chapters.content:
Chapter 1

The target, a petite blonde in her twenties, walks out the main door of a small office complex. She’s dressed in business casual attire, off work for the day. Less than a dozen parked cars are scattered throughout the lot in front of the building. She spots her blue Honda sedan and heads towards it.

The sun has just begun to set, so the parking lot lights have not come on. A thick mix of hedges and palm trees border the lot, providing privacy from a low-traffic road nearby. The target unlocks her Honda and gets inside. Once situated, she tries starting the ignition. The battery’s dead. She tries again but gets nothing, not even a click. In sudden frustration, she wrings her hands and fishes her phone out of her purse. She stops when she hears a car approaching.

A silver Porsche Cayenne pulls up and parks in the spot beside her. She looks through her window and sees the driver, a moderately pretty blonde who’s roughly five years older and potentially helpful. The target drops her phone back into her purse and scrambles to get out of her car. She goes around to the driver’s side door of the Cayenne.

Inside, Shay Fontaine is turning off the ignition. When she opens her door, Shay is greeted by the flustered blonde.

“Hi there. I am so sorry to bother you, but do you have jumper cables by any chance?” She presses her palms together in front of her chest, practically pleading.

“I do, actually.”

The target tilts her head back in relief. “Oh, thank you.”

Shay gets out of her Cayenne and pops open the back hatch door. As she walks around back with the target at her side, Shay bumps her elbow on the backseat window.

“You okay?”

“Yeah,” Shay nods, “just clumsy.” They arrive at the back hatch door where Shay takes out a set of jumper cables.

“Great. I’ll go pop my hood.” The target darts over to her Honda.

“All right.” Shay circles back around to the front end of her Cayenne. She peeks into the backseat window before opening the driver’s side door. Shay reaches in to tug the hood release lever. She leaves the door open.

“Okay, it’s me first, right?” The target props up the hood of her car and meets Shay in front of the Cayenne.

“Right, the red one.” Shay hands her one end of the jumper cables and lifts her hood. “Will they reach?”

The target holds up the cables. “Yes they will.” She hooks the red clamp onto her battery and sees Shay following in suit. “Thanks again, by the way.” The target attaches the black clamp onto a bolt on the engine block and gushes to Shay. “I really appreciate this.”

“It’s okay. It happens.” With a kind smile, Shay goes around to the driver’s side door of her Cayenne. She leans inside to start the engine.

The target gets into her car while Shay lingers nearby, standing between the two vehicles. The Honda’s driver side window is cracked. Shay steps closer to the car. She slips her hand inside the pocket of her hoodie, waiting for an opportunity.

“I left my lights on.” From inside the car, her voice is muffled.

Shay stoops down to the driver’s side window and knocks on it. “What’d you say?”

The target rolls down her window and repeats herself. “I left my lights on.”

“Oh...well, try it out.” Shay suggests and browses the parking lot. She doesn’t see anybody else around. The parking lot lights still haven’t come on. Beside her, the Honda’s engine starts, and the target sighs in relief.

Shay takes her hand out of her pocket. She’s holding a folded white cloth. She reaches inside the window and covers the target’s mouth with the cloth. A muted scream fills her palm as Shay uses her free hand to block the target’s flailing arms. Shay manages to grab the target’s right wrist while pressing the cloth into her face. She looks down at the frantic brown eyes staring up at her.

Stomping her feet on the floor mat, the target tries to push Shay’s hand off her mouth, but the anesthetic effects take hold of her. Weaker by the second, she can only manage to cling onto Shay’s forearm, and even that is short lived. Her turbulence subsides.

Shay repositions her fingers on the target’s right wrist to track her pulse. The target’s left arm droops down into her lap. Her eyelids flutter shut. Shay leaves the cloth over her mouth a couple seconds longer for good measure. She kicks out her leg and thumps the rear door of the Cayenne a couple times with her boot.

Diligent, Shay opens the car door and shoves the white cloth back into her pocket. The target’s body is slumped over towards her center console. Shay locates the seat adjustment controls and wiggles the toe of her boot under the lever. The seat begins to recline.

Trip gets out of the backseat of the Cayenne. Following the game plan, he walks around to the rear passenger side of the Honda and climbs into the backseat. He pushes the front passenger seat forward to open up some room. The driver’s seat, holding the target’s limp body, reaches its fully reclined position. Shay pulls her foot out of the car and shuts the driver’s side door. She heads off to remove the jumper cables and stow them back away in her Cayenne.

From the backseat, Trip slips his hands under the unconscious target’s arms. With a grunt, he drags the upper half of her body over the headrest. Her wilted arm slides down the side of the driver’s seat. Trip shifts forward, bracing himself on the backside of the passenger seat. He ducks down to grab the backs of the target’s knees, tugs up on her legs and rolls her body into the backseat. She lands on her side with her knees bent.

Shay closes the hood and gets in behind the wheel of the Honda. She feels around for the adjustment lever and raises the seat back up. In back, Trip takes a moment to catch his breath and survey the unconscious blonde. She’s his age, mid-twenties.

Shay reaches over the center console to push the passenger seat upright. “Make it look like she’s taking a nap.” She glances at Trip in the rearview mirror.

“It already looks like she’s taking a nap.” He chuckles. Trip arranges her arms more naturally, bending her elbows in front of her chest.

“You know what I mean.” Shay smiles at him. “Make it look like she’s passed out, in case I get pulled over or anything.”

“I think this is as good as I can do.” Trip gets out of the Honda.

“All right, I’ll see you later.” Shay waits for him to close the door and head over to her idling Cayenne. She backs out of the stall and drives out of the parking lot. On her way, she passes by the office complex. There’s a lit window on the ground floor.

***

Inside that lit office on the ground floor, on matching cream-colored couches, Becky Martin sits across from a middle-aged, homely therapist. Thriving plants fill the windowsills. Onyx rugs cover the polished oak floor. The balance of contemporary décor rooted by earthy elements creates a comfortable office setting.

“It’s nice meeting you, too.” Becky tucks a strand of golden blonde hair behind her ear with a French-manicured nail. She acts completely impartial about her therapy session.

“So Becky, tell me why you’re here today.” The therapist has a notepad resting on the arm of her couch and a shiny silver pen in her hand.

“My mother was in town for a short visit last week and thought I seemed,” she finishes her sentence with a trivializing shrug, “disconnected, was how she put it.”

“But you don’t agree?”

“Nobody except for my mother would look at my life and think, ‘yeah, that girl needs therapy’.”

“Why do you say that?”

“Well because, I have a steady job and I live in a decent place. Which isn’t always easy to do in L.A.” She contends. “I don’t have a criminal record or any addictions, nothing like that. I’m not depressed.”

“What are you?”

“If anything, I’m bored.”

The therapist nods, touching the tip of her pen to the notepad. “What did your mother notice that made her think you needed to talk to somebody?”

“It’s really nothing new.” Her focus drifts over to the woodgrain essential oil diffuser dispersing a lavender mist on the other side of the room. “It’s the fact that she still sees me the same way she did a decade ago, when I went off to college. And I’m not the same person anymore.”

“Was there something more specific, for her to ask you to come here?”

“My general attitude towards life, I guess. My boyfriend, Brian, is a complete jackass. Just to give you the most recent example, he was supposed to come over for dinner last night, right? Dinner was made, candles were lit, and what does he do?”

“What?”

“He gets too drunk to drive over, which I don’t find out about until I call to ask him why he’s late.” Becky frowns as she goes on. “He’s a shallow, self-centered drunk with Peter Pan syndrome and it’s really just a matter of time, to be honest.”

“What keeps you in the relationship with Brian?”

“That’s a good question. As bad as it sounds, I’m probably waiting to move on, when I have someone to move on to.” Her gaze travels to the plants in the windowsill. “You really don’t have to tell me how insecure and wrong that is. I already know. It makes me sound as shallow as him.”

“We can revisit that relationship later. Tell me what else is going on.”

“Okay, I’m twenty-nine, so naturally I’m at that stage where everyone I know is either getting married or having babies. That can be annoying.”

“Annoying how?” the therapist asks while making a note.

“Like my co-worker Jackie inviting me over for ‘sangria and centerpieces’ because half of her bridesmaids are totally unreliable. Don’t get me wrong, I love Jackie, but I’m not one of her bridesmaids.”

“So did you go?”

“It’s happening right now, so no, I don’t plan to. Actually, I’m glad you had an appointment open up so that I could come take care of this tonight.”

“So, I understand you’re frustrated with several of your relationships right now, but was there a specific catalyst that alarmed your mother last week?”

“It was the dream. I don’t even know why I told her about it.” Shaking her head, Becky reaches for the coffee table between them. “Won’t make that mistake again.” She picks up her open bottle of water and has a sip.

“The dream?”

“I’ve been having this bizarre, recurring dream. It makes absolutely no sense to me, but it’s very vivid.”

“Can you tell me about it?”

Becky sets the water back down on the coffee table and warns her. “It’s weird.”

“I understand.”

Becky takes a deep breath, lifting her brows. She unfurls in a relaxed manner. “I wake up in this cellar...”

Thick metal shackles are bolted to the curved brick wall, down in the bowels of the circular underground cellar. Becky is stripped down to her underwear, cuffed to the wall. It’s so dim down there that only her silhouette and movements are fully visible. She thrashes her arms around, fruitless. Grunts of anger spill out of her mouth as she attempts to break the chains.

There’s a stone staircase directly across from her. It leads up to a candlelit balcony level, once used for seating at wine tastings. Between clashes of metal against brick, Becky hears something. She stops moving, her breath is a pant.

Up above on the balcony, two indistinguishable men appear. They stand at the wrought iron railing.

Becky looks up at them. “This is enough! You stop this, right now!” She grabs the chains and throws them against the brick wall behind her. Her voice is hoarse from screaming. “You’re on my territory. This is MY kingdom!” As the echo of her voice dies down, Becky hears the distinct sound of a fly being unzipped. Her eyes widen in horror. “Oh, no you don’t. Don’t you dare!” she screams out. The reverberations of her cry grow weak...

“I know. It’s weird.” Becky holds her hands up to the therapist.

“Dreams often are.” She jots down notes. “Do you know who these two men are?”

“No, that’s the thing. I never see their faces. Dreams are funny like that. Sometimes you know that you’re dreaming about a certain person, but it doesn’t look like that person, you know?”

“Yeah.” She nods at Becky.

“Well, not only are their faces a blur, but I have no idea who they’re supposed to be. But in the dream, I definitely know who they are.”

“Not all dreams involve people you know, even though they do come from the subconscious.”

“Right.” Becky uncrosses and re-crosses her legs in an antsy gesture but maintains her unruffled façade. “So what do you think?”

“It sounds a bit to me like your subconscious is struggling with a loss of control. Like, you’re fighting to hang on amid the internal battles you’re dealing with.”

Becky teeters her head in consideration of the therapist’s observation.

***

Shay drives the Honda down a seemingly deserted road. When she comes up onto a slight hill, a cluster of trees appears on her left. She digs her phone out of the pocket of her hoodie and makes a call. “Hey, I’m pulling in.” She ends the brief call and immediately makes another one. Shay’s inflection on the second call is notably more commanding. “I’m almost there. Get ready to take the car. I’ll leave the key in there. You have the address, correct?” Satisfied, Shay ends the second call and slips her phone back into her pocket.

She turns into the long driveway leading up to the palatial Mercer Estate. Shay follows the curve around to the side of the house, which is illuminated by landscape ground lighting.

Two men walk out of the side entrance door, Reno and Random. They’re both of average height and athletic build, both attractive, but Reno has a particular appeal. Random is carrying a lightweight stretcher under his arm. He is the picture of composure; he’s calm, assuming and in complete control.

Shay reels back in her seat, blown away at the sight of Random outside to fetch the target. She pulls the car up next to them and shuts off the engine. When Shay gets out of the car, Reno and Random approach the passenger side.

Reno glimpses overtop the car at Shay while she pushes the door shut. “Where are we taking her?” he asks and peers down into the window at the blonde target’s body in the backseat. “Is this number seven?” He opens the rear door.

“Yup, number seven.” Shay’s normal gregarious demeanor emerges. She walks around the car towards them, still astonished to see Random doing grunt work. “Wow, I got you two to unload?”

Random sets the stretcher on the ground.

“And to stage.” Reno informs her. Random stands across from Reno in front of the open car door.

“How generous of you,” Shay says specifically to the head honcho, Random. She leans against the side of the car and watches them.

They each take a leg and begin pulling the unconscious body out of the car.

“How’d you drain the car battery in the first place?” Reno asks her. They get the bottom half of the target’s body slid out far enough, and then both reach inside to grab one of her arms.

“Oh, we didn’t.” Shay explains. Hanging by her arms and legs, the blonde is carefully lowered down onto the stretcher. “He stopped there himself after lunch and turned on her headlights and interiors. He has a key, obviously.”

“That makes sense.” Reno nods. He and Random grip the handles on either end of the stretcher. They pick it up and start carrying it towards the house with Reno leading the way. Shay pushes herself off the car and hustles ahead of them to get the door. She opens the side entrance door for them. They pass by her, going down a set of concrete steps. Reno and Random move steadily down the staircase with the stretcher.

Random glances up over his shoulder at Shay in the doorway. “I trust there were no problems.”

“Of course not.” Shay steps inside and pulls the heavy door shut behind her. She follows them down the stairs. The unadorned basement corridor has numbered doors on both sides. “Her suitor is supposed to be here in about a half hour if someone can babysit.”

“I can do that.” Reno offers. When they reach the bottom of the steps, he keeps backing up until Random has enough room to turn the stretcher down the quiet corridor.

Shay jogs ahead to a metal door that has the number 7 on it. “And Trip’s at her apartment waiting for her car to be dropped off.” She turns the handle and opens it for them. Random and Reno rotate the stretcher in front of the door and head inside.

“Are you going, or are you sending someone?” Random asks as he passes by Shay. He walks through the doorway.

“Hell no, I’m not going. My job here is all but done.”

Chamber 7 is small and simple with eroded cinderblock walls and cement floors. Two thick chains dangle from a large eyehook bolted into the wall. Candle sconces cast a faint glow around the dank little dungeon. There’s a purple velvet chair in the corner.

Next to the purple chair is a rolling cart that holds an arranged row of items: a coil of rope, a flogger, a ball gag, a paddle and a handful of clothespins. A wooden stock sits in the middle of the chamber. The handmade detention unit is a hinged stock, to trap the neck and wrists, which connects to a sturdy pillory frame with a horizontal kneeling board.

Shay walks inside just when Reno and Random are setting down the stretcher. She spots the ominous wood device. “Perfect, you remembered the stock.”

“Did you think I’d forget?” Reno has an offended crinkle in the corner of his eyes. “That’s the equivalent of me asking if you remembered to get the contract signed.”

“Fair enough.” Shay notices his sexy sneer.

Random stays out of their banter. Crouched over the target’s body, he and Reno begin removing her clothes. Reno takes off her sandals while Random unbuttons her thin cardigan sweater.

Shay stands near the doorway. “What’s on the menu tonight?” She pats her stomach through her hoodie. “I’m starving.”

“It smelled like Mexican fare.” Reno tosses the sandals aside and starts a clothing pile. He moves up her body to the waistband of her linen pants.

“That works for me.” Shay watches Random open the front of the thin cardigan. “I’m sure you know what to do from here.”

“All under control.” Random bends the target’s elbow. He pulls her arm out of the sleeve of the cardigan. Across from him, Reno is unbuttoning her linen pants.

“I’ll be upstairs, then.” Shay exits the chamber. She sets off down the basement hallway, breezing by the numbered metal doors, 5...3...1. She passes by the staircase that leads up to the side entrance door and continues into an eerily dim, open area where she approaches an elevator. Her phone rings. She pulls it out of her pocket and answers the call. “Why hello. Yes, she’s almost ready for you.” Shay punches the ‘up’ button on the elevator. “Okay then, enjoy your evening.” She smiles. “Oh, I’m sure you will, too.”

The elevator doors open.

***

“Do you think you need to start seeing me on a regular basis? Or anyone for that matter?” the therapist asks Becky, who shakes her head. Their session is wrapping up, signaled by the timer on the essential oil diffuser across the room turning the unit off.

“No, not to be rude, but I don’t. I just don’t think therapy is what I need.”

“What do you think you need?”

Becky hesitates before answering, “An alternative. I don’t want to just do what everybody else is doing.”

“Do you know what sort of alternative?” She touches the tip of her shiny silver pen to her notepad.

“Not yet, but I’ve got my eyes open.”

Becky’s obscure comeback prompts a more direct final question from the therapist. “So, what are you doing currently to cope with your feelings about where you’re at in life?”

***

White wine flows from the bottle into an empty glass. At her townhouse, standing in her galley kitchen, Becky sets down the bottle and picks up the wineglass. She snatches a torch lighter off the end of the quartz counter and walks into her dark living room.

A laptop computer screen casts its subtle light across a neatly kept desk. Becky uses the torch lighter to light a couple of pillar candles on her computer desk. Her laptop chimes with an incoming message. She smiles and says to herself, “I knew it.” Becky settles into her desk chair and opens the chat message from a user named Stillborn. She slides her glass of wine onto the desk and reads the message.

Stillborn: Have you rethought the cam request?

Becky, who’s signed onto the screenname HelloKitty69, types her reply.

HelloKitty69: still thinkin bout it, k?

She clicks ‘send’ and tenses up. Almost in a panic, Becky begins typing a new message.

HelloKitty69: But plz dont go. Havent heard from u lately n rly wanna talk to u.

Becky picks up the glass of wine and rocks back in her desk chair, riveted on the screen. The computer chimes. She reaches forward to hit the ‘mute’ button on her keyboard.

Stillborn: Ok. This time. My patience is running thin.

“Good.” She takes a small sip of wine and sets the glass back down. Hands on her keyboard, Becky starts typing.

HelloKitty69: I know and I promise soon.

Stillborn: What do you want to talk about? And type in real words so I don’t feel like I’m talking to a teenager.

HelloKitty69: Deal. Last week, my mom asked me to make a therapy appt, right? Because that’s where honesty gets you, sent to therapy.

Stillborn: Only in your world

Becky huffs before she continues typing.

HelloKitty69: So the appt was tonight and it went fine cos I followed ur advice

Stillborn: TYPE IN REAL WORDS. THIS IS WHY I’M ASKING FOR THE CAM.

HelloKitty69: Sorry. So the point is, I never got mad. Mom was just worried, now it’s done. I didn’t attach any emotion to the event.

Stillborn: Oh, so you’re finally reading the lame articles I’ve been sending you.

For the past two months, ever since Becky signed up on this adult site and started talking to this Stillborn character, he’s been sending her the occasional introspective article.

HelloKitty69: I’ve been reading them at work. I never said they were lame.

Stillborn: You definitely did.

Becky smiles. She tucks a strand of hair behind her ear and resumes typing.

HelloKitty69: Maybe the first time. I was probably a little drunk. Anyway, I didn’t just read them. I understood them and even applied them.

Stillborn: And they worked. It’s just about changing the way you think.

HelloKitty69: Yeah, something about you makes sense finally.

“For once.” Becky sips her wine, and the computer screen flashes. She locks in on the incoming message on her monitor.

Stillborn: I guess it’s time to change tactics then, before you figure me out.

HelloKitty69: That’s it? That’s all you have to say?

Stillborn: You expect praise for taking good advice?

The doorbell rings. Becky gasps in surprise. She minimizes the chat window on her computer screen and sees the time. It’s 11:20. When Becky stands up from her desk chair, the doorbell rings again. She spins around and rushes over to the window. It’s Brian. He’s out on the front porch making a funny face at her through the glass. Becky rolls her eyes and opens the door.

A clean-cut guy with a charming grin, Brian walks into the shadowy living room and closes the door behind him. “Why’s it so dark in here?”

“What are you doing here?”

“Rob dropped me off.” Brian points over his shoulder at the door.

“Okay, but why?”

“Cause I wanted to see you.” He wraps his arms around Becky’s waist, looking past her at the computer screen. He’s drunk and giddy, but still coherent. “What, are you busy or something?”

“No, but it’s almost eleven-thirty, and we have to work tomorrow.” Becky catches a whiff of the alcohol on his breath. “And you are trashed.” She wiggles out of Brian’s hold and backs away from him.

“So what?” He can see the wineglass on her desk. “Like you’re not?”

“I’m not, actually.” She glances over at her monitor. A new message notification flashes in the lower corner of her screen. “But it’s still late.”

“So we’ll go to sleep together. What’s wrong with that?”

“Listen Brian, at least go brush your teeth. Feel free to take a shower too, but the teeth are mandatory.”

“You’re selfish today.”

“I’m self...” Becky cocks her head while Brian stumbles along into the bathroom. She hurries back over to her computer, clicks on the new message and types a reply.

HelloKitty69: My idiot boyfriend just staggered in. Sorry.

She deliberates for a moment before clicking ‘send’. Becky closes out the chat window. She hears Brian gargling in the background. Becky swivels her chair and yells towards the bathroom. “It’s truly amazing that you make it into work every day!”

“I’m amazing.”

With a grumble, Becky leans back in her desk chair and begins rocking.

***

The sound of canned laughter rings out from a TV mounted on the wall above an unlit stone fireplace. The TV is the only light source in Black’s spacious master bedroom, his sanctuary in his suite within the Mercer Estate. A tan wingchair sits in the corner next to the fireplace, near a large window covered with chocolate brown drapes.

On the wall across from the fireplace is a rich four-poster bed with 12”x12” fluted square wood posts. Black is lying on the bed, propped up against the padded headboard. Comfortably dressed, he has dark eyes and a stoic face. He sets his laptop aside on the bed. He’s holding a lit joint between his fingers. A phone and remote control are sitting on the nightstand by his bed. The phone vibrates, so he picks it up and answers the call. “Shay.”

“What are you doing? Are you here?” she asks.

“Yeah, I’m here.”

“So he just left here to take her home. How do you feel about tackling chamber cleanup?”

“Which one?” He takes a hit of the joint.

“Seven, it’ll be super easy.”

“I guess I could do that for you.” Black’s apathetic tone harmonizes with his facial expression.

“I would appreciate it. I’ve done like, eight of these scenarios in the past two weeks.”

“You’ll owe me one.”

“You know I’m good for it.” Shay avows.

“I know.”

“Thank you, Black. I’m calling it a night.”

“Okay.” He ends the call and snuffs his joint out in a white porcelain ashtray that’s sitting on the bed beside him. He moves the ashtray over to the nightstand before rolling off the bed.

Black walks out of his bedroom and turns the corner into a quiet living room area. A floor lamp softly lights the room. The TV screen on the far wall is off. Plush taupe drapes are drawn over the two tall, narrow windows on either side of the screen. A modern, steel grey sectional faces the TV, filling the center of the living room. Black cuts across the dark-stained hardwood floor to the front door of his suite. He slips on a pair of shoes, opens the door and heads out.

He steps into the wide penthouse corridor. With décor-free beige walls and stylish light sconces, it resembles a hotel hallway. Black pulls his door shut behind him. The word ‘Entropy’ is mounted on the outside of his door in routed, gold leaf letters.

“Hey Black!” Trip calls out to him from further down the corridor.

Black pauses and waits for Trip to catch up with him.

“Have you tried out the new strain?”

“I just did.” He nods at Trip. “Literally.” The two of them go on down the hall towards the elevator, centrally located in the long corridor.

“I’m on my way down now. How is it?”

“Well, I let Shay pass off chamber cleanup to me, so...”

“Ah, okay.” Trip smiles. “That’s a good sign.” They arrive at the elevator where Trip bends forward to punch the ‘down’ arrow. He vacates the elevator on the first floor.

When the elevator doors open to the basement level, Black comes out alone. The doors slide closed behind him. He walks through the underground corridor of chambers, passing the numbered metal doors. On his way, he pulls his phone out of his pocket and makes a call.

Black reaches for the knob and opens the door to chamber 7. He steps inside the doorway, holding his phone up to his ear. “Grab a couple people for a cleanup in number seven.” Black visually assesses the post-scene situation. The wooden stock is in the middle of the dank chamber. There are no spills, no trash to collect, and the play items on the rolling cart by the purple velvet chair appear to be unused. “It’s not bad. Just put the gear away, wipe down the stock, move it back to the arsenal and mop the floor.” Black scans the chamber. “Yeah, that’s it.” He glances over at the purple chair. “Oh, and check the chair cushion, just in case.”

***

The next morning, Brian is at his desk, working on his laptop. Though it’s a modest-sized office, he does have a window behind him that overlooks the WPC courtyard area down below. Brian’s co-worker and friend walks into his office and sits down in a chair across the desk from him.

“Hey.” Rob is an easygoing, average Joe. “How was your night?”

Brian continues typing as he talks to Rob. “Meh, boring.”

“Boring?”

“Becky was being a bitch, like I interrupted something.” He blows it off. “I don’t know. I just crashed, honestly.” Brian stops to pick up his coffee mug and take a sip. He sets the mug back down and resumes typing. He’s been doing this job long enough that he can seamlessly type a detailed quote while carrying on a conversation.

“Let’s cut early for lunch.” Rob suggests.

“Sure, let me just finish this bid.” He furrows his brow. “I seriously need to find something different.”

“What do you mean?”

“Well, it’s like... How long have I been seeing Becky, anyway?”

“Uh, about six months, maybe. Don’t you know?”

“That seems right.”

“Here we go again.” With a knowing groan, Rob leans his head back on the wall behind him.

“No, see, that’s just it. I don’t want to keep doing the same thing, because I keep winding up bored at the six-month mark.”

“I’ve noticed that pattern. I think everyone around here has.”

“I’m almost done with this.” Brian scrolls back up to skim through his work. “Anyway, I know that I do not want to keep cycling through co-workers, here.”

“Right.” Rob sounds jaded.

“No, I’m serious. But I don’t know whether to wait it out with Becky while I look for something else, because I’m not really sure what I’m looking for yet.”

“So just wait it out. Becky’s not that bad, in my opinion.”

“That’s only because you see ‘happy drunk Becky’.”

“I see Becky every day.” Rob motions down the hallway. “She works right down the hall.” He thumbs out the doorway towards the WPC reception area...

The front reception area is open and tidy, with an oak receptionist desk situated in the center. The WPC logo is mounted on the wall behind the desk. A hallway runs straight down each end of the reception desk. Potted floor plants border the entrances to each hallway.

Brian’s open office door is visible from the reception desk where Becky stands talking to Jackie, who’s wearing a headset and sorting through a stack of mail.

“How’d sangria and centerpieces go?” Becky asks her.

“I’m a little hungover, but we got them done.”

“That’s good news. I’m sorry I couldn’t make it.”

“Oh, it all worked out.” Jackie reassures her with a wave. She’s a young and bubbly Hispanic who, fortunately for Becky, does not hold grudges. Jackie is to Becky what Rob is to Brian, a friend as much as a co-worker. The multi-line phone blinks with an incoming call. Jackie reaches to answer it.

“I’ll catch you at lunch.” Becky pats her hand on the counter and heads for the hallway to her office. When she hears Brian talking, she stops and lurks behind one of the tall potted plants at the end of the hallway.

“I just don’t know if I can do it,” Brian says.

“Do what, exactly?”

“I don’t know if I can wait for the Becky thing to run its course, or not.” Brian and Rob arrive at the end of the hallway. They don’t notice Becky step out from behind the floor plant. “I need to break the cycle.” Brian freezes in mid-step when he sees Becky standing in front of him. Rob’s jaw slacks.

“That makes two of us.” Becky notifies him, projecting her patent resolution.

Though clearly caught off guard, Brian makes no effort to retract his statement.

Becky folds her arms. “If I find anything of yours at my house, I’ll bring it in to work.”

“I’ll do the same.”

“Great. Well, good luck. God knows you need it.” Becky twirls away from Brian and walks off down the hallway to her office.

“That was really rude, man,” Rob says quietly.

“Me or her?”

Rob frowns at him. “You.”

***

Becky and Jackie are sitting at a picnic table eating their lunch in the WPC building’s courtyard area. It’s a mild and sunny day, typical of May weather in southern California. Jackie is halfway through a sandwich. Becky stabs a fork into a container of pasta salad.

“Have you ever had a dream that’s so vivid, you wake up thinking it actually just happened?” she asks Jackie.

“Yeah, but I don’t remember any of them now.”

“Well, I’ve been having this dream that I’m being tortured by these two guys.” Becky has a bite of her pasta salad. Jackie crinkles her nose.

“What two guys?”

Becky shrugs. “I don’t recognize them.” She proceeds to tell Jackie about being chained to the brick wall and how the two men come inside and stand above her on the balcony that runs all around the inside of the round cellar.

“Sounds more like a dungeon.”

“It is like a dungeon. So anyway, they come in.” Becky waves her fork around, animating her story. “And I start yelling at them to stop, and that it’s my kingdom.”

“Your kingdom?”

“Yeah, I don’t know what it means. Then they,” Becky trails off, “they do something, and I wake up.”

“What do they do?” Jackie picks up her can of soda and takes a drink.

Through a laugh, Becky says, “I’m pretty sure they’re gonna start pissing on me, but I don’t stick around for that part.”

“Oh, sick!” She sets her soda can down on the table with a thud of disgust.

“I know. It’s driving me crazy.”

“Let’s talk about something else, then. What was going on with Brian earlier? I heard you guys talking.”

Becky takes a cleansing breath as she prepares to spill the story. “I heard him tell Rob that he didn’t think he could, ‘wait for the Becky thing to run its course’.”

Appalled, Jackie’s eyes bulge. “No.”

“Yes.”

“What? What the– why did you not open with this?”

“I haven’t exactly been excited to talk about it.” Becky sheepishly looks down at her pasta salad. “It wasn’t a pleasant thing to hear, you know?”

“I know, but you went on with your nightmare about being pissed on and never thought to mention that you and Brian broke up?”

“It was gonna happen sooner or later. It’s not that big of a surprise.”

“Yes it is. You were supposed to be the one who ended it.”

Becky stiffens at Jackie’s words. “Ouch, I know. I’m not saying that I’m not upset, but still.” She mechanically pokes her fork around inside the container.

“Oh my God.” Jackie whispers in a daze. “I cannot believe he said that.”

“He obviously wasn’t too concerned. He knows I could’ve heard him. If he cared–” Becky stops herself midsentence. “But of course, he doesn’t care.” She stabs her fork into the cold pasta with heightened aggression.

“It never ceases to amaze me how big of an ass he can be.”

“And how people just, put up with it. That’s what amazes me.”

“Uh-huh.” After an awkward silence Jackie asks, “So, are you still meeting up at Tiger’s after work tonight?”

Becky answers with a flat, “No.” She tilts her head. “Are you being serious?”

“Well, we’re your friends, too. I mean, just because Brian’ll be there doesn’t mean you can’t come.”

“It means I don’t want to.” Becky rebuts irritably. She rests her fork down inside the plastic container. “I realize that Brian’s escapades are common knowledge around here, but I’m not gonna just accept it and hang out with everybody like nothing’s wrong.”

Jackie begins collecting her things. “I just don’t see why you have to be the one who avoids social situations.”

“It’s by choice.”

“I guess that’s up to you, then.” She swings her purse over her shoulder. “Hey listen, I have to call my mom on my way back in.”

“Okay.”

Jackie gets up from the table. “And seriously Becky, good riddance.”

Becky nods at Jackie and watches her leave the courtyard area before spying up at Brian’s office window in the WPC building. Since the situation with him has thrown a wrench into Becky’s normal Thursday night plans, she picks up her phone to search for something else to do.

***

A small, spring Arts & Crafts Festival is being held in the downtown area. Food vendors line the street, which is barricaded off from traffic. A savory mix of spices and grill smoke float through the air. Colorful tents are intermixed throughout, most with goods for sale. Paintings, pottery, soaps and jewelry are all available for purchase. Off to the side of the main drag is a bright red fortune teller tent.

Inside that tent, Becky is seated across from a psychic, an older woman whose mousy brown hair is piled up on top of her head. She’s dressed in a flowing jade-colored robe. Tapestries line the inside walls of the tent. The mismatched lamps in the corners add a soft mystique.

“I can’t help but notice you have a tense aura. Did something happen to you today?”

“It was a stressful day.” Becky admits.” I broke up with my boyfriend.” Tarot cards are arranged on the round, cloth-covered table between them.

“Oh, is that why you’re here?”

“No, it really wasn’t serious. I’ll get over that. I’m here to find out what’s going to happen.”

“Well, this is present day.” With a pearly fingernail, the psychic taps the Four of Cups tarot card. “The Four of Cups generally indicates discontent.”

“That’s appropriate.” Becky centers on the next card in the sequence. “What does The Magician represent, then?”

“This is someone in your life, who you may or may not already know. This person will show you a new direction.”

Becky looks up at the psychic, intrigued by her words. “Really?”

“Could this be someone you already know?”

“It could be.”

“Who do you think this person is?”

“It’s kind of a long story.” Becky’s focus reverts to the cards. “So do I go in the new direction?”

The psychic nods. “Looking ahead, it seems as though you do take this new path.”

“Oh great,” Becky mutters when she sees the next card in line, The Hanged Man. “And then I’m doomed.”

“I don’t think that you’re doomed, as much as you’re changing your perspective from here to here.” The psychic taps her fingernail between the Magician and the Hanged Man. The Temperance card is in-between these two. “This jump indicates that your outlook has changed significantly. Once you arrive here to the Hanged Man, you’re simply suspended. Where you go from here is too ambiguous right now. This will be a rebirth of some kind, further down the road.”

“Can we back up a little? I’m wondering why this jump even happened.” Becky points at the Temperance card, sequentially before the Hanged Man. “Because Temperance doesn’t seem too bad. That just means I need to like, moderate my behavior, right?”

“It means more than that, Becky.” The psychic hovers her hand over the Temperance card. “It means this is a time when you will try and blend opposites that may not mix. I suspect your efforts will lead to the change in perspective that follows.”

“So while I’m trying to mix oil and water there, I’m going to be punished for my actions here.” Becky refers to the Hanged Man card.

“Punished, stopped, redirected. The synthesis you will try to achieve will not work, because your goal or ambition is not realistic.”

Becky’s forehead wrinkles in a palpable attempt to wrap her mind around the premonition.

***

Later that evening, Becky runs on her treadmill in the bedroom of her townhouse. Her hair is pulled up into a ponytail, and her skin shines with light perspiration. She runs to clear her head, but the perplexed glower on her face depicts that it’s not working.

The bedroom is a decent size. It comfortably fits her queen bed and nightstands, in addition to two dressers and of course the treadmill, which is on the wall across from the door. A TV sits on the shorter dresser across from Becky’s bed. The mini blinds on her windows are drawn closed, blocking out the night sky.

Becky hops onto the side rails of the treadmill and turns it off. She pulls a water bottle out of the front holder and wipes off her face with a small towel before stepping off the machine. Becky walks out of her bedroom into the living room and over to her computer desk. She glances down at the open chat message to Stillborn on her laptop screen.

HelloKitty69: It’s finally over with Brian. Hope to catch you.

There’s no response to her message. She sets her water bottle on her desk, slumps down into her desk chair and sighs in frustration.

“Oh, come on magician. Please have nothing better to do tonight.” She reaches for her keyboard and fires up a card game to distract herself while she waits. The Hello Kitty clock on the wall above Becky’s desk reads 9:40 p.m.

***

Black’s windowless office in his suite at the Mercer Estate is pitch dark except for the glow of his laptop sitting on the desk. He steps inside and looks down at the screen. After a contemplative beat, Black makes a phone call. He stands in the doorway of his office with his phone to his ear. “Hey, are you busy right now? Then would you mind stopping by so I can get your opinion on something?” He nods. “Yeah, I’ll have a Jameson neat. Thanks.” Black walks out of his office and through the low-lit living room to the front door of his suite. He slips his phone into his pocket and opens up the door. A distant conversation is taking place out in the penthouse corridor. The voices grow faint. A few moments pass by.

Random appears in Black’s doorway. “So you have something to run by me?” He steps inside the suite, carrying a distinct air of prominence along with two glasses of whiskey.

“Yeah.”

***

Still planted in front of her computer, Becky mindlessly plays her card game in the dark living room. Finally, she hears the chime of an incoming message. She minimizes the game and zeroes in on the chat message box on her screen.

Stillborn: Congratulations. You’re through the phase. Go to this link and turn on your cam.

“Really?” She begins typing a response.

HelloKitty69: Don’t you want to know what happened?

Stillborn: Not really. Go to the link.

HelloKitty69: Gimme a minute.

“Oh no.” Becky stands up from the desk chair, rigid and frazzled. She dashes into her bathroom and flips on the light. The mirror reflects her wiped-away makeup and disheveled hair. “So not prepared for this.” She tears off a section of toilet paper and blots her face. It’s no less blotchy than it was before. Becky tosses aside the toilet paper and starts running her fingers through her tousled hair. Painfully dissatisfied, she proceeds to pull her hair back, combing it smooth with her fingers. She picks up a hairband and hears the distant chime of an incoming message. Becky drops the hairband on the bathroom counter. She rushes back into the living room.

The glow from the computer screen illuminates Becky when she sits down at her desk. She reads his most recent message.

Stillborn: I’m through messing around.

“Okay.” Becky scrolls further up in the chat message window and finds the link he sent. She clicks on it. Two windows open on her screen. One displays a live feed of Becky’s face and the other, Black’s. She takes in her first sight of the broody dark-haired man and his compelling energy.

Her image is in color, while Black’s is in black and white. But Becky doesn’t notice this right away. She fixates on Black’s deep, intense brown eyes...quietly studying her. Becky vacillates between nervousness and anticipation.

“Hi.” She sinks back in her chair and smiles.

“Turn on your mic.”

Becky flinches at the sound of his low, imposing tone. “Oh.” She reaches forward to turn her mic on.

“That’s a good kitty.” Black smirks at her.

Laughing self-consciously, she looks up at her Hello Kitty clock on the wall, the artless inspiration for her handle. “I know. It’s a dumb name.” Becky concedes to him on the screen. She finally notices that his image isn’t in color. “How come you’re in black and white?”

“That’s just my theme. It’s a little esoteric.”

“Oh,” Becky tosses her head back in bemusement, “so you actually do talk like that?”

“Like what?”

“In riddles!”

“Does that surprise you?” he asks with a shrug.

Becky fidgets with the hem of her flannel shorts. The reality of seeing the Magician’s face for the first time brings the situation to a new level. “You know,” her gaze wafts down in reluctance, “I realize this isn’t that big of a deal and all.” Becky glances back up at the screen and signals to her image timidly. “But I’ve never done anything like this before. I honestly don’t do this.”

“Then why do you have a camera?”

“It’s built into my monitor. But I’ve never really used it, because–”

Black cuts her off. “Because you’re not that type of person, right? Discretion and common sense are the main things I like about you Becky, but we’re still just online.”

“Right.” Becky’s pang of apprehension recedes. “I know.” She acknowledges his point. “And I do appreciate your patience with me.” She squints. “I guess.” As she talks to him, Becky eases into the moment. “I mean, I know there’s no way that all of this is just about getting laid.”

Black scoffs at the absurdity of Becky’s statement. “If I were just looking to get laid, I would’ve shelved you two months ago. I want to meet you because I can show you something a lot more interesting than what you’ve been doing.” He speaks with natural confidence and a smooth stride. “I also think you know that life has a lot more to offer, don’t you?” He questions Becky to break her out of her spacey stare.

She nods at him, concentrating on his attentiveness.

“And you want to see what that is.” He confirms.

Becky marvels at Black’s persuasion. A curious twitch pulls at the corner of her mouth. “I really think I do. Against my better judgment, as it very much is.” She clarifies for him as if it’s necessary. “Because you know that nothing you’ve ever said about your life makes any sense.”

“But something makes you trust me.”

“Something does.” She agrees and sees his mischievous glint. “Or maybe I’m just going through some period of insanity.”

“No, insanity is doing the same thing over again and expecting different results.” He gives his slightly altered version of Einstein’s definition.

“I’ve heard that one before.” She confesses, shying away from the debate.

“So I guess something I’ve said makes sense.”

Becky glimpses up at his calm face. “Something definitely makes me interested, which I’m sure you can tell.”

“Well,” Black says nonchalantly, “you’d always wonder what you missed out on. If you never take the chance.”

“You’re probably right. I just wonder if, whatever this is, might be more than I can juggle into my life.”

“Trust me. I won’t leave any questions unanswered. But some answers will have to come with time.” Black speaks his cryptic words with upmost certainty. “And I’ll roll the dice that the day will come, when you thank me for coming into your life.”

Becky arches her brows at his bold claim. She mulls for a moment before replying. “It’s crazy. I believe you, and I can’t believe half the words coming out of my own mouth, lately. But for some reason, I believe you.” She relaxes into a smile.

“It’s the chance for real freedom. I have it, and you want to see what it’s about. So you listen to me, in spite of your conditioned reservations.” He asserts. “Just admit it and agree to meet me.”

“When?”

“Check your email from home at exactly three o’clock tomorrow.”

Becky scrutinizes Black, waiting for him to continue. “That’s it?” She grimaces. “You’re not gonna tell me where we’re going or anything?”

“Kitty, this marks the beginning of the tricks I’m teaching you. So no, I’m not telling you anything except to check your messages tomorrow at three.”

With that, Black disappears from the window on Becky’s monitor...

In his office within his suite at the Mercer Estate, a still shot of Becky’s bewildered face is visible on Black’s laptop screen.

“Why do you bother with her?” Random asks, severely underwhelmed.

“I know she seems like a challenge.” Black turns away from the laptop. He’s in his black leather desk chair. Wall lamps softly light the long, narrow office. “But I’ve got a gut feeling.”

“Really?” Random has been sitting behind Black on a tall barstool, eavesdropping on him and Becky. He reaches for his whiskey on the round pub table beside him. “You’ve been dicking around with her for two months already and just finally talked her into getting on camera.” Random shakes his head. “I’ll put money on it she backs out before you even get her to a party.” He sips his whiskey.

“Not a chance.” Black retorts, thoroughly self-assured. “Mark my words. Becky Martin’s gonna take it all the way.”

“You really think so?” Random’s skepticism is pronounced.

Black motions over his shoulder at Becky’s image on the monitor. “You saw her cave.”

“Yes, but with unyielding resistance, right up to the end when she bitched about not knowing where she’s going tomorrow.”

“That’s the spirit I’m after.” Black bares a surreptitious smile.

“So then...” Random discerningly connects the dots. “You’re not looking for a sub.”

“At first, of course. And I think she’ll do okay at the bottom if I keep promising her more. But once she starts thinking for herself–”

“Aha.” Random interjects, containing his enthusiasm. “That’s when she’ll launch.” He huffs at Black. “Well, that changes everything. I obviously didn’t know your intentions because this one’s a worthless sub recruit.” He scans Becky’s image with newfound appeal.

“Oh, I agree completely. She’s way too aggressive.”

“What’s your plan?” Random asks.

Black reaches for his drink on the desk, which sits against a brick wall in the dimly lit office. Further down the lengthy desk is a pair of additional monitors. “Well, she’s expecting a sex game of some kind.” One of the extra monitors displays a split-screen divided into four sections. Each section shows a black and white feed from each of Black’s subordinate quarters, basic bedrooms. “So I’ll play along with that, initially.”

“Sure.” Random nods in forgone conclusion.

In one of the four sections on the monitor, a pair of blonde twins (Marsa & Minya) watches television in a queen-size bed. Another section shows a younger woman (Kayleigh) wrapped in a towel, combing out her wet hair. In the third one, is the back of a woman’s head (Kaime). She’s seated at a corner desk, picking up a glass of red wine. The fourth section is empty.

“And I’ll start breaking the impatience, immediately.” Black affirms. “She’ll be a quick study.” He takes a small drink of his Jameson, which he’s barely made a dent in.

“What all does she know at this point?” Random’s attention wanders down to the far end of the office. Hanging on the wall is an abstract erotic painting of a woman’s bare torso on the back end of a panther, done on a black velvet canvas.

“Very little, I’ve kept the conversation light,” Black answers.

“Where’d you meet her, again?”

“She signed up on one of the kink sites, claiming she was bored.”

“Hmm.” Random hums pensively. “She’s cagey.” He glances up. Along the ceiling border of the office’s brick walls, a quote is painted in white letters. It reads, ‘The mind of the party is collective and immortal’ with a credit to George Orwell below it.

“But she’s persistent.” Black counters Random’s remark.

“True, and you’ve gotten her this far along. She does want to meet you.”

Black smiles. “Boredom really brings out the best in people.”

Random shrugs in concurrence before asking, “So you’re doing a job tonight, aren’t you?”

“Yeah, leaving for it shortly.”

“I’ll let you get to it.” Random slides off of the barstool and picks up his empty glass. He casually adds, “If you need my help with anything.” He gestures to the image of Becky on Black’s laptop screen. “Just let me know.”

“Okay.” Both surprised and interested, Black follows Random out of the office.

“I wouldn’t mind getting a closer look and interacting with her myself, you know?” Random heads for the front door.

“I might take you up on that sooner than later, actually.” Black steps ahead of him to pull the door open.

“Sure, let me know.”

“I will. Boredom really does bring out the best in people.” Black quips.

Vaguely amused, Random leaves the suite.

Black turns away from the door, leaving it open. The TV is on in his living room, but the volume is down low. Black walks from the front door to his steel grey sectional. His phone rings in his pocket. He pulls it out and answers the call. “Hannah.”

“Are you all set for tonight?” Her bossiness rings through the phone. “Any questions or anything?”

“Well yeah.”

“What?”

“Do you have supplies for me?” Black has a seat on the sectional, facing the TV.

“Reno’s loading you a backpack. He should be there any minute. Other than that, you’re all set?”

“Just waiting to leave. If all goes well, it should be a quick in and out. Twenty minutes tops, plus drive time.” He skims the TV in front of him.

“Right, when there’s no abduction involved, they’re a piece of cake.”

“Usually.” Black ruminates. “I’d feel a lot better if I had a copy of her key, though.”

“I know. Like I said, Joe has the key to her individual apartment, but not for the main door. And you obviously can’t have her buzz you in.”

“I don’t like the alternative of going through the patio door in the first place, especially with no key.”

“At least it’s ground level.” She snaps back with tenacious optimism.

“And locked.” Undoubtedly conflicted about this detail, Black sets his phone on the coffee table in front of him and puts it on speaker.

“I know. Joe said he could not get a key to the patio door.”

“That’s unfortunate.”

“Trust me, I agree. But in a way, it’ll make it more believable.”

“Okay.” Black chortles.

“Anybody in here order a break-in kit?” Reno enters the open doorway into the living room. He’s carrying a black backpack.

“There he is.” Hannah’s voice booms out of Black’s phone.

Reno walks around to the front of the sectional and hands the backpack to Black, who sets it down on the floor between his feet.

“I put all the lock picking stuff in the front pocket.” Reno relaxes into the couch. He lights a cigarette and tosses his pack down on the coffee table.

“Reno, could you reassure Black that patio doors are not that hard to get into.”

“Depends on the door, but it shouldn’t be too bad based on the picture of it Joe sent.” Reno takes a drag of his cigarette. He watches Black unzip the front pouch of the backpack and rifle around inside. “I put all kinds of stuff in there.”

“Yeah, I see that.” Black zips the front pouch closed.

“Nothing to worry about.” Hannah pipes in.

“Goodbye Hannah.” He reaches forward and ends the call.

Behind Black, out in the penthouse corridor, Trip passes by the open door. Upon hearing Black inside, Trip backs up and stands in the doorway. “Hey, I just stopped down and had Ankh roll me one.” He holds up a Dutch style, cone-shaped joint.

“Bring it in.” Black raises his arm, inviting Trip to come inside. “Want something to drink?”

“What do you have in here?”

“I don’t know.” Black directs him to the kitchen. “Have a look.” He does not typically stock his suite’s food and beverages.

“So what are you guys doing?” Trip walks past the sectional into the kitchen.

“Checking out my supplies for a break-in,” Black answers.

“You’re doing a scenario tonight?” he asks and opens the refrigerator.

“I am.” Black leans back down over the backpack. He unzips the top to rummage around inside the main compartment.

“It’s all in there.” Reno ensures him and flicks his cigarette into the white porcelain ashtray on the coffee table.

***

The target’s apartment complex is a three-story brick complex in a middle-class neighborhood. Black is hunched over the handle of a glass patio door. The backpack is slung over his shoulder. He’s wiggling a pick into the keyhole but can’t find the release. He crouches down to get a better angle, tries again, and hears the ‘tick’ he’s waiting for.

Black stands back up and slips the pick into the front pocket of the backpack. He cautiously slides the patio door open, steps inside the apartment and slides the door shut behind him. While walking into the dark living room, he pulls a black ski mask down over his face. Paired with his leather jacket, Black is looking pretty menacing tonight. He creeps into the hallway and notices the TV on inside the bedroom.

He stands outside the bedroom door and listens. Upon hearing the heavy breathing of sleep, he pushes the door open and walks in. The target, Michelle, a brunette in her early thirties, is fast asleep under a down comforter. She’s lying on her side with her back to Black. He takes the backpack off his shoulder and slowly unzips it. He feels around inside and withdraws a roll of duct tape. Black calmly pulls out a strip, tears it off and sticks it to the sleeve of his jacket.

After setting aside the roll of duct tape, Black digs into the backpack for a coiled rope. He finds an end and circles around to the side of the bed, facing Michelle.

She has one arm splayed out on the bed in front of her. The other is tucked under her pillow. Black bends down to slide the end of the rope under Michelle’s available wrist. He carefully pulls the rope through and ties a slipknot.

Assuming that Michelle will wake up when he goes for her other wrist, Black takes the strip of duct tape off of his sleeve. He wraps the tape over Michelle’s mouth, which results in her eyes blinking open. Before she has a chance to process the situation, Black reaches under her pillow and grabs her other arm. He loops the rope around her wrist, binding her hands together.

Michelle lets out a stifled squeal. She tries to roll away from him. Black jumps onto the bed and straddles her squirming body, pinning her down. He pauses upon hearing the distinct sound of the patio door opening in the living room.

“Oh shit...”

Michelle stops squealing. Black drops the rope and leaps off of her bed. He pushes the ski mask up over his forehead and backs away from the bed, where Michelle is wrestling her wrists out of the rope.

A stocky forty-something guy in sweatpants storms into the bedroom, holding a gun aimed at Black.

chapters.title: Chapter 2
chapters.content:
Chapter 2

The guy in sweatpants flips on the bedroom light and points the gun at Black’s chest.

Black raises his arms, showing his empty hands in surrender. “This is not what it looks like, I promise you.”

“Hmph!” Michelle waves at the guy to stop as she peels the duct tape off of her mouth. “Barry, it’s okay. He’s getting paid to do this.”

Taken aback, Black stares down at her. “Do you know me?”

“Well, no, but I think I know what’s going on.” Michelle rubs her face where the tape was. “It’s not my first time.”

Mystified by this chain of events, Barry gradually lowers the gun. “What?” he asks incredulously.

“I’m fine, really.” Michelle looks him straight in the eye. “There’s no need to involve the cops, or anything like that.” She professes to him.

The concern fades from Barry’s face. “If you’re sure.”

“I am.”

“That’s probably good, it’s not like I have a license for this.” Barry admits and slips the gun into the waistband of his sweatpants.

“Go on back home. And thanks for watching out for me, and everything. I’m sorry for all this.” She sends Barry a warm smile.

“No, I’m just glad everything’s okay.” Barry turns to leave the bedroom.

After a lull, Michelle peers up at Black. “So do you want to call Joe, or should I?”

“Please.” Black extends his open arms to her. “Be my guest. He’s just parked down the street.”

“Oh, okay.” She nods. “Wow, sorry that got so messed up, there.” Michelle starts looping the rope up around her hand.

Still distraught, Black bends down to pick up the backpack. He circles back around her bed to the bedroom door. “I’m gonna leave through the front door.” He firmly states.

“Sure, sure.” Michelle holds out the rope. “Did you want this back, or anything?”

Standing in the doorway, Black glances back at her. “Keep it.” He exits the bedroom.

***

Later, Black walks into his bedroom and peels off the leather jacket. He fishes his phone out of the pocket before tossing his jacket down onto the floor. On his way over to his four-poster bed, Black pulls up a contact on his phone, SAM - AMS. He calls her.

Black sits down on the edge of his bed and holds the phone up to his ear. He hears her cranky morning-voice on the other end of the line.

“What?”

In a droll monotone he replies, “Good morning dear.”

“Good morning Black.” She sounds groggy.

“Did I wake you?” he asks...

“Not really.” Sam is sprawled out on an off-white couch in the living room of her Amsterdam flat with her phone to her ear. Morning sun seeps through the closed blinds in a paned window behind the couch. She’s a brunette in her late twenties with engaging eyes and a naturally pretty face. Sam clears her throat. “This is just the first time I’ve talked today.” Her trim figure is hidden beneath a Sherpa throw. She reaches for a cappuccino sitting on the coffee table in front of her. “So what do you want?”

“I had a close call tonight.” Black relays impassively.

“What do you mean by that?”

“I could’ve got shot.”

“What?” Instantly alarmed, Sam sets her cappuccino back down on the coffee table. “What happened?”

“It was a scenario, a break-in gone bad.”

“A break-in gone bad?” She reiterates.
