“Thanks.” Random reaches out to take the pen and clipboard back from her. “You have a good afternoon.”

“Thank you, you too.” Becky closes her door and picks the three gifts up from the table. She carries them over to her desk to check them out.

First, she opens the envelope and pulls out a folded sheet of thick grey paper. Becky opens it up and reads the letter:

Number one, Real time is the black, the normal. Virtual time is the white, beyond the normal. And right now you’re in the grey area, which is an invitation to play a game that takes you from the black into the white. The farther you go, the greater the reward. That’s the one and only promise I’ll make. So before we go any further, let’s make sure neither of us is wasting our time. I need you to think about the things we’ve talked about and ask some questions.

The letter is signed, Black.

With a deducing nod, Becky flicks the corner of the letter. “Black. Black and white theme.” She refolds the letter and slips it back into the envelope. Her incoming email alert sounds once again. She turns her chair to the monitor. Clicking open the email from Black, she devours the message:

Reply to this email and ask me whatever you need to know. Once I give you the answers, number two is what you’ll use to indicate your consent. Should you decide to play, number three is what you’ll wear when we meet later. Now get your questions out of the way so we can get going.

Becky’s lips twist into an eager grin. She closes the email window and unwraps the black box. Inside the box is a supple white leather thong. After giving it a judgmental snort, she tosses the thong aside on her desk and clicks the ‘reply’ button on the email.

***

Meanwhile in the living room of Black’s suite, he, Trip and Reno are spread out around the steel grey sectional. His front door is wide open. Buoyant reggae music plays in the background.

“Think you can help me out with that later?” Black asks Reno.

“Yeah, I was planning on being there tonight, anyway.” Reno lights up a cigarette.

“Her name is Becky, just to get that out of the way.” Black advises him.

Hannah cruises into the living room from the penthouse corridor and heads towards them. “Hello.” She joins Black on the couch, leaving a cushion’s width between them.

“You’re back. Why?” he asks aloofly.

“I’m just killing a little time, is all.” Hannah sets her phone down on the coffee table and eyeballs Reno. They swap a spirited sneer of contempt.

“The time-killing room.” Trip digs in his jeans pocket for a lighter. He has a joint in his other hand.

“Squandering is one of the many joys of hedonism.” Reno watches Trip not light the joint. He takes a drag of his cigarette.

“I smell coffee.” Hannah turns to Black. “Where are your subs at?” she asks, hinting at the expectation of being served a cup.

“The twins are downstairs in the lounge. Today’s their birthday.”

“Oh, that’s right.” She sounds bummed. “I guess I’m not gonna make it to the club tonight.”

“I don’t think they’ll notice.” Black gestures to the hallway on his left, at the bedroom doors. “I think the other two are just in their rooms.”

“I really hate to miss a V.I.P. party at the club, but.” Hannah slaps her hands on her thighs, pushing herself back up into a standing position. “Priorities, you know?” She disappears into the small kitchen to get herself a cup of coffee. The thud of a cupboard door closing is followed by the clink of Hannah setting a coffee mug down on the granite kitchen counter.

“What time is it?” Trip wonders out loud.

Black glances over at Hannah’s phone on the coffee table to check. “Almost five.”

“What time are you lighting that thing?” Reno points the tip of his cigarette at the joint in Trip’s hand. “Huh?”

“Oh.” Trip looks at the joint absentmindedly.

Hannah walks back into the living room carrying a mug of coffee and returns to her seat on the sectional near Black.

Further down, Reno waits for Trip to light up the joint, take a couple of puffs and hand it to Black. “Finally.” He sets his cigarette in the ashtray and stretches his arm out in front of Hannah to take the joint from Black.

She sips her steaming coffee and sets the mug down next to her phone. “I think I’m gonna go the strip club route this time around.” Hannah announces, signaling her desire to talk about her impending subordinate hunt.

“For what, recruiting?” Reno asks while holding his hit.

“Yeah,” she answers with a hint of distaste about the chore. Reno offers her the joint. “No thanks.” Hannah declines. “I’ve gotta stay sharp.”

Trip stands up and leans over the coffee table to take the joint back from Reno, who’s on the opposite side of the sectional from him.

“Hannah’s on a mission.” Black teases her.

“Oh, that’s right.” Reno passes the joint to Trip. “Your new minion bailed already, didn’t he?”

Hannah emits a weary sigh. “Yeah, yeah.”

“You’ve gone the strip club route before though, right?” Reno settles back into his seat.

“I have. It’s always prosperous. Kind of like my shortcut.”

“May as well take it, then.” Reno scoffs. Alongside his cigarette smoke, the stench of weed has overtaken the coffee scent in the living room.

Behind Black, Shay appears in the open doorway.

“My phone won’t stop ringing.” She hangs onto the doorframe dramatically.

“Shay, you need to start delegating more of the game plans for these jobs out to us.” Reno sways to the thumping reggae beat.

“Oh please.” Hannah derides him with a huff. “I love how you offer while you’re sitting on your ass getting high.”

Reno gazes at her, stoned. He slants forward to snuff out his cigarette.

“It’s been a crazy couple weeks.” Trip agrees. “Income tax refunds, maybe?”

A ripple of laughter passes through the living room.

“You’re probably right, though.” Shay nods at him. “I keep thinking I’m caught up, and then I get another damn call. It’s not easy being me.”

“Give me a break. You’re addicted.” Trip accuses her and sees the terse smile that Shay gives him in response.

“Are the chamber four people still here?” Hannah asks her.

“Yes, they’re here.” Shay lets go of the doorframe and flops back against it. “But my end is done.”

“Who’s getting stuck with cleanup?” Black looks over his shoulder at Shay.

“Cade.”

“Glad to hear it.”

“I wouldn’t ask you twice in a row, Black. I don’t want to owe you too many favors. You cash ‘em in.” Shay grins at him.

“You should go down and get a massage,” Hannah tells her. “Unwind.”

“Funny enough, that’s exactly where I’m heading.”

“Enjoy. Bye.” Hannah flutters her fingers at Shay, who exits the doorway. Propping her feet up on the coffee table, Hannah peers over at Black. “Where is Cade, by the way? I’m surprised he’s not in here.”

“Oh, he’s busy.”

“Doing what? Working on his super-secret plan?” She mocks.

“Yeah, I think so.”

“His what?” Reno is clueless.

Hannah, the only lucid one in the room at this juncture, keeps the conversation rolling. She turns to Trip. “Guys seem to like you, Trip. Maybe I should have you recruit somebody for me.”

Trip doesn’t respond, spaced off in his own little world.

“I guess that’s a ‘no’.” Reno chuckles at Trip’s trancelike state.

Black checks the time on Hannah’s phone on the coffee table. He gets up from his couch and stands near the front door in silent encouragement for his guests to leave.

Oblivious to Black’s innuendo, Trip snags his lighter from the coffee table and mumbles, “I’ve got to go check on something.” He has a distracted frown on his face.

Reno and Hannah exchange a what-the-hell glance. “Everything all right, there?” Reno asks him.

“Fine, I just remembered something.” Trip stands up from the sectional and roams to the door in a haze. He passes by Black on his way out.

Black looks at Reno with a shrug that denotes he has no idea what’s come over Trip.

Hannah picks her phone up off the coffee table. “I should head off, too. I need to get mentally prepared to be,” she takes a deep breath, “charming, tonight.”

“No time to waste, then.” Reno jibes.

“No time to waste with you, that’s for sure.” Hannah counters insipidly. “You’re almost as bad as him.” She homes in on Black over by the door.

“So bitter, Hannah.” Reno grabs his cigarettes from the coffee table. He stands up and aims a feisty snarl at her. “It just kills you knowing that I could round somebody up tonight without even trying.”

“And you think I can’t?” Hannah retains her dignity while he attempts to pluck her nerves.

“You really think you’ll recruit one tonight?”

“Sure do,” she answers confidently.

“How much do you want to put on it?”

“Let’s say, two no-questions-asked favors.” She proposes.

“You got it.” He strolls across the dark hardwood towards the front door.

“It’s on.” Hannah springs up and follows him.

“I’ll start thinking about what I need done.” Reno continues his snarky banter with Hannah as they make their way to the door.

Black is waiting by the suite door with his hands shoved in his pockets.

“Try not to get lost on the way back to your suite while you do that.” She rolls her eyes.

“My fully staffed suite.” Reno highlights, sauntering out into the penthouse corridor.

Hannah steps up to the doorway and stands across from Black.

“Good luck tonight,” he tells her.

“Thanks. I need it now that I’ve got a wager with Reno.”

“I’m sure you’ll be very motivated.”

“You don’t know the half of it. And you,” she lightly pokes Black in the chest, “have a good night tonight. I’d tell you to have fun, but it’s you, you know.” Hannah refers to Black’s reserved disposition. “Nonetheless, I hope everything goes swimmingly.”

“We’ll see.”

“Tell the twins I said Happy Birthday.”

With a soft laugh through his nose he says, “They wouldn’t believe me. You better tell them yourself.”

***

Minya walks into her bedroom in Black’s suite holding an armful of dresses. Her sister Marsa is sitting cross-legged on the bed. She has her hair up in hot rollers. The flaxen-haired Egyptian twins are leisurely getting ready for their birthday celebration. With wideset blue eyes and plump lips, they have an exotic appeal. They appear dreamy and stoned even when they’re completely sober; Marsa, more so than her sister.

A vase of fragrant white roses with a Happy Birthday balloon tied around it sits on the nightstand. The twins’ phones are next to the vase. Minya walks past the nightstand and slides a pile of dresses off her arm onto the bed. Marsa looks up from filing her nails at the heap of dresses at the foot of the bed.

“Okay, I’ve gone through both our closets. I think I have it narrowed down to three dresses.” Minya bends down to start sorting through them.

Their queen-size bed is shoved into the corner of the small bedroom, leaving just enough room next to it for the nightstand and a long dresser along the wall opposite from the bed. A full-length mirror is propped up between the closet and the bedroom door. Their carpeted floor is scattered with shoes, cosmetics, hair products and a few colorful gift bags.

“What’d you find?” Marsa tosses the nail file down on the nightstand. She reaches up to re-secure a hot roller in her hair.

Minya pulls out a cream sheath dress. “Is it corny if we match?” She sets it off to the side.

“Oh no way, we have to match tonight.”

“That’s what I thought, too.” Minya heads over to the closet. “I could only find one of the cream ones in your closet, so I’m guessing the other one’s in here.” She opens the closet door.

Marsa scans the two rectangular gift boxes on the dresser. Both are wrapped in glossy black paper, trimmed with white satin ribbons. “Black had me wrap your gift.”

“Same here. I didn’t get to see what it was, though.”

“Neither did I,” she imitates Black, “you are not to look inside the box, Marsa.”

Minya giggles at her sister and shoves a section of clothing out of her way inside the closet. “He had me wrap something else too, a box for Becky.”

“Who’s Becky?” Marsa bristles.

“Some outsider, I don’t know.” She flips through hangers.

“Is he trying to recruit her?” Prying for information, Marsa rummages around inside a cosmetic bag full of nail polish bottles.

“He’s obviously pursuing her, but I don’t really know any details. Never a dull moment around this place.”

“I know. That’s why I love it.” Marsa settles on a bottle of diamond polish.

“I can’t find the other one.” Minya sounds frustrated. On the nightstand, both phones beep simultaneously with an incoming message. “Who is it?” Minya peeps over her shoulder at Marsa on the bed. She’s reading the messages.

“It’s Black. He says to open our gifts.” Marsa transitions to a whisper. “Do you think he’s listening to us?”

“Probably.” Minya goes over to the dresser and picks up the two black boxes. Recognizing her handiwork on the bow, she hands Marsa her gift. “This one’s yours.” Minya leans against the dresser and unties the satin bow on her own gift. The twins open up their boxes and pull out matching silky, scarlet dresses.

Marsa gasps. “This is gorgeous!” She holds up the spaghetti straps of the revealing yet elegant dress.

“I guess we know what we’re wearing tonight.” Minya sets the box on the dresser behind her.

***

Becky also knows what she’s wearing tonight. Sitting at her desk, she bounces back and forth between the white thong lying next to her keyboard and the email from Black, his response to the list of questions she sent him that afternoon. She scrolls through his reply email one last time before closing out the window and standing up from her desk chair. Without looking down at it, Becky picks up the leather thong on her way to the bathroom.

She walks in and shuts the door behind her. She loops the white thong around the neck of a plastic hanger which is holding a black cocktail dress, following in line with his black and white theme. Becky hangs the dress up on a silver hook on the back of the door next to a pale pink robe. She takes her phone out of her pocket, pulls up her workout playlist and sets her phone down on the bathroom counter.

Uplifting, repetitive techno music plays faintly through Becky’s phone as a backdrop to the Q&A email she just finished reading for the third time. Her first question to him was, ‘Are there any major changes I’ll need to make in my daily life to play your game?’

Becky heads over to turn on the shower. She backs away from the tub and brushes out her blonde hair.

For one, you had to miss a few hours of work today to get my message. Things like that will come up now and then. You might think about making up a lie to use in reality, for times that you need to get away without telling the truth.

She brushes her hair up into a ponytail. Her second question was, ‘What exactly does virtual time mean?’

The shower fills with steam while Becky undresses.

At the risk of sounding vague, that’ll be entirely up to you.

Becky pushes the textured glass shower door closed behind her. The fuzzy silhouette of her body is visible through the shower door. She begins washing her face. Her third question was, ‘Are there any safety issues I should be aware of?’

My lifestyle doesn’t involve any sort of brainwashing, cult activities, or even intoxication that isn’t consensual. It’s all about trust and common sense.

Inside the shower, Becky rinses soapsuds off her face. She lathers up a terrycloth bath glove and starts soaping up her neck and shoulders, working her way down her body. Her fourth question was, ‘How would I get out of this game, if I had to at some point?’

If normal-life circumstances get in the way, you just have to let me know. There aren’t any strings attached on my end.

She stands under the showerhead, letting hot water run down her body. The joyful beat of the synth techno song intensifies. Her fifth question was, ‘What might make you get rid of me at some point?’

Wrapped in a towel, Becky walks up to the fogged over bathroom mirror. She steps in front of the sink to brush her teeth.

Disobedience is what would end the game. Because if you accept the invitation, then you’re agreeing to do what I ask while we’re playing. With your consent, comes your trust.

She pulls a curling iron from a lower cabinet and plugs it in. While the iron heats up, Becky reaches for a bottle of lemon sugar body lotion. She pumps some out and spreads it over her skin.

Keep in mind that your role in this will always be changing. So if there’s a part you don’t really like, something different is around the corner. As long as you can take the bad with the good, you’ll eventually get to make rules instead of obey them.

Becky slips into her pale pink bathrobe and leaves the bathroom. Her sixth and final question was, ‘What made you choose me for this?’

She heads through the golden rays shining into the living room, over to her desk and picks up the white rose.

Your screen name begged for attention, so I struck up a conversation. I’m pretty good at reading between the lines.

Rose in hand, Becky walks to the front door and opens it to a view of wispy clouds over the setting sun.

Now, when you’re ready to accept, put the rose out on your porch.

The white rose lands in the corner of her porch.

Don’t forget gift number three. I don’t care what you wear over it, but we’re going to a club where I know a lot of people, so aim high.

Becky is nothing if not meticulous about her appearance. In the hour it takes the sun to fully sink down into the horizon, she is onto finishing touches in the bathroom. Her blonde hair hangs in loose curls. She adjusts her black cocktail dress before reaching around her back to zip it up. Her makeup is done. Becky is ready to go. After swiping a silver bangle bracelet from the counter, Becky flips the light off and leaves the bathroom.

Be ready to go at eight o’clock. That gives you plenty of time, so take advantage of it.

She passes through her dusky living room, sliding the bracelet onto her wrist. On the wall above her desk, the Hello Kitty clock reads 8:00.

The doorbell rings. Becky slips her feet into a pair of black sandals. She grabs her handbag and rushes to open the front door. On the far corner of her front porch, the white rose is gone.

chapters.title: Chapter 3
chapters.content:
Chapter 3

After she acknowledges the white rose missing from her stoop, Becky looks up from the porch at her ride.

“Becky?”

It’s not Black. It’s a handsome dirty blonde in his thirties, wearing an olive suit.

“Yes, I’m Becky.”

“I’m Ryan. I’ll be driving you to dinner.” Behind him, a silver sports car idles in her driveway.

“Ryan.” She repeats, a little stunned. “The driver?”

He nods at Becky, asks, “Ready to go?” and extends his hand to her.

If you accept the invitation, then you’re agreeing to do what I ask while we’re playing. With your consent, comes your trust.

“Yes I am.” Becky takes his hand and follows him down to the humming car.

Ryan the driver is cordial during their short ride to dinner. He keeps the conversation as minimal and vague as possible within the constraints of courtesy. After seeing Becky to the front door of Luciano’s restaurant, Ryan drives off in the silver sports car.

Nothing about the night ahead is divulged, yet it’s all very organized and specific. A svelte, middle-aged hostess steers Becky through the upscale Italian steakhouse. They arrive at the round table draped with a white tablecloth where Black is seated. Two empty wineglasses and an ice bucket sit on the candlelit table.

The hostess pulls out the chair across from Black, who greets Becky with a socially expected smile. Becky looks right back at him while she gracefully slides into the chair. She acts like she’s playing it cool, but Becky’s seething with excitement. The hostess leaves and is replaced right away by a waiter approaching their table with a bottle of Vouvray. He presents the bottle, partially sheathed in a white cloth napkin. Black nods at the dutiful young waiter, who begins the uncorking process. He removes the cork, hands it to Black and pours a small taste into Black’s glass.

After approving the wine, Black turns to Becky. “Welcome.”

“Thank you. It’s nice to meet you.”

The waiter fills each of their wineglasses halfway before placing the bottle into the gold ice bucket on their table and walking away. Becky picks up her wineglass. She scans Black’s charcoal grey dress shirt, his dark hair and clean-shaved face. In person, his charged vigor is amplified.

“Have you ever been here before?” he asks her.

“No, but I’ve heard of it.” Becky glimpses up at the vaulted stained-glass ceiling that glows in warm rust-orange shades. “You know what it reminds me of?”

Black shakes his head.

“Have you ever been to Fleming’s Grill? It’s down on Forty-Fifth Street, I believe.” She sips her wine.

“We’re not on a date. You know that, right?” Black wags his finger through the air between them. “This isn’t a date.”

“Okay.” Becky freezes, holding her wineglass out in front of her.

“So you don’t need to make idle remarks. I’ll take care of the conversation.” He relays before changing the subject. “Did you have any trouble getting out of work today?”

“It was short notice, but I have plenty of PTO hours so it was no big deal.” She sets her wineglass down. “And by the way, I already have a lie I can use in the future, to get away.”

“Tell me what it is.”

“Sure, but I’ve got a quick question.” She waves her hand over the table. “Normally there’s a menu.”

“I turned our order in earlier.”

Becky balks in surprise. “I see. What am I having?” she curtly asks.

Black leans back in his chair and casts his eyes down on her. “Why don’t you answer my question first?”

“Fair enough.” She concedes. “Like I said, I’m a step ahead of you on the whole ‘lie’ deal, for a totally unrelated reason. Last month I got promoted to a new department at work, so I planted the seed that I have a handicapped sister. Which I do, but she lives with my parents in Phoenix.” Becky curls her fingers around the stem of her wineglass. “I didn’t mention that part, though.” She takes a larger sip of her wine.

“And why did you do that?”

“That’s the funny thing. I did it because Brian’s in the department that I got promoted to. So, if I ever needed to get out of an awkward situation, I could use my sister as an excuse.” With a tightlipped smile she adds, “Ironic, huh?”

“Convenient. Fortunate, even.” He lingers in thoughtful silence until Becky breaks it.

“How about telling me something about yourself, Black?” She razzes him. “Like your real name, for instance.” Her frisky attitude is not well received by Black.

“Because who I am and what I do isn’t really important at the moment.”

“What if I want to get to know you a little better?”

“Oh you will.” Unflappable, Black tilts his head at Becky across the table. “Just not in the same ways you’re used to getting to know people.” He continues in a stanch voice. “And I should tell you, this dinner is really informal. I don’t want to overwhelm you or anything, so I’m keeping things light right now.”

“Oh, go ahead and overwhelm me.” She invites him with a flirtatious beam. Becky takes another drink of wine, draining her glass.

“When I say right now, I mean that.” Black’s tone turns patronizing. “Never fear kitten, I’ll hardly bore you. But my role in this game is to set your pace. And you can’t run a marathon without any training, because you’ll set yourself up for a loss.”

“Okay, okay,” Becky playfully butts in, “I get the metaphor.” She notices Black’s lean body straighten up and tower over the table towards her.

“Yeah, that right there,” he says in an assertive posture, “once we get up from this table, won’t be tolerated. Do you understand that?” He waits for Becky’s round-eyed nod. “Don’t test that.” Black relaxes back into his chair. Becky’s fluster fades into a coolheaded expression that demonstrates her understanding of the act he’s putting on. It’s a role-playing game.

“I apologize. When I don’t know the rules, it’s hard to play the game right.” She explains.

“Well for starters, don’t be yourself.” He gets straight to the point. “When I told you I wanted to show you off to some friends tonight, it’s not so they can weigh in on a potential girlfriend.” Black’s raw words are somewhat soothed by his calm delivery.

“Okay, I understand that.” Becky claims and then retreats inward, attempting to process what he’s saying.

A food server approaches the table with their meals. The waiter follows behind him, refilling Becky’s wineglass.

Black thanks the waiter and turns back to Becky, picking up where he left off. “And number two, quit trying to run the show. I’m not here to put up with your cheeky little bullshit attitude.” He picks up his fork. “So just shut up, clear your mind and eat your steak.”

His command leaves her speechless. Becky reaches for her silverware and cuts into her filet mignon.

***

A cobalt blue halter dress hangs from the shower door in the master bathroom of Hannah’s suite at the Mercer Estate.

“Will!” Her impatient shout reverberates off the walls. “Where the hell is he?” she asks under her breath. Hannah, wearing a fluffy white robe, pivots over her vanity with an eye pencil in her hand. Focused on the mirror, she accents her smoky shadow by penciling in a dark streak just past the corner of her lash line.

“He’s not in here.”

Hannah glances back at Trip in the doorway, rattled by his presence. “Oh.” Her blonde hair cascades down her shoulder in flowing waves. “Do you happen to know where he is?”

“I saw him downstairs getting something to eat.”

“Okay. And what are you doing in here, if you don’t mind my asking.”

“I wasn’t in here. I could hear you yelling from the hallway.” Trip gestures behind him.

“Oh. Sorry.” She turns back to the mirror.

“So, did you need something?”

Hannah uses a cotton swab to soften the line she drew at the corner of her lid. “Grab me a Xanax. They’re in my nightstand.”

“Are you nervous?” Trip chuckles and turns away from her bathroom door. He walks into the adjacent master bedroom.

“No, I’m still reeling with the whole ‘putting Black’s life at risk’ ordeal. I just don’t want the distraction tonight.”

“Yeah, Shay told me about that,” he says from the other room.

“I figured she had.” Hannah pitches the cotton swab. “You know why it’s such a big deal when I make a mistake? Because I don’t usually make them.” She spots Trip in the mirror’s reflection, holding out his hand. “Thanks.” Hannah twists around to take the pill from Trip’s palm. She sets it down on the light-colored granite vanity and looks at his image in the mirror. He’s looking back at her.

“Where are you going tonight?”

“Rumors,” she tells him.

“I’ve been there. When are you leaving?” he asks.

“I don’t know, around ten.” Hannah spouts. “What are you doing? I thought everybody left for the club by now.”

“I’m waiting for a phone call before I head over there.”

“Something important?” Her edginess wanes.

“I don’t know yet.”

An inquisitive twitch crosses Hannah’s face. Earlier that evening, Trip had grown distracted for unknown reasons and left Black’s suite in a fog. “Does it have anything to do with earlier?”

“What?” Her question baffles Trip.

“In Black’s suite, when you got all constipated and said you had to go check on something. Remember?”

“Oh, yeah, actually it does.”

“Is everything okay?”

“I don’t know yet.” He spaces off, similar to the way he did earlier. Hannah catches it but lets the subject drop.

“Okay, well I hope things go the direction you want them to, then. I guess.”

“You too.” Trip snaps out of his funk. “Tonight, I mean.”

“Thanks, Trip.” Hannah watches him disappear from the doorway on his way out of her suite. She leans back into the mirror muttering, “Kooky kid.”

***

Back at Luciano’s restaurant, Becky stabs her fork into her last bite of steak. She pops it into her mouth and sets down her fork.

“Tell me what you’re thinking right now.” Black picks up a fresh rum and cola.

“I’m not sure you want to know.”

“Dammit, Becky.” Shaking his head, Black sips his drink.

“All right.” She backs down. It’s obvious that he wants her to be subdued, but it’s equally obvious that she’s not sure how to go about it. “The temptation to challenge and exceed expectations is in my blood. So right now, I’m wondering how I’m supposed to just repress my natural instincts.”

“Stop juggling your faith with your doubt. Just observe.” Black takes another drink and sets his glass down on the table.

“See, I don’t know what you mean by that.” Becky picks up the wine bottle. “What do I like, tell myself, you know?” She pours the last splash of wine from the bottle into her glass.

He nods in understanding and dumbs it down for her. “Separate the game like you separate any other situations in life. You play a certain role when you’re with your family. And you play a different one when you’re out at the bar with your friends, right?”

“Yes.”

The waiter shows up at the table to deliver their dessert, cherry cheesecake, then vanishes.

Black picks up his fork and carries on. “I’m sure you know the term ‘work mode’. Think about how you already play other roles. Take away what you talk about and focus on how you act around certain people, in certain situations.” He eats a bite of his cheesecake and watches Becky follow in suit. “This is just a different act. So, push everything out of your mind and go into ‘anticipation mode’, all right?”

“Okay.” Becky blinks at him a few times. His explanation allays her. She washes the bite of cheesecake down with the last of her wine.

“When I tell you to shut up and do what I ask, don’t get offended.” He lets out a short laugh. “Just do it. That’s all you have to concentrate on, me and my directions. That’s it. Your role’s easy.” Black sets his dessert fork down on the table and tosses his cloth napkin over the plate. “You did a good job, by the way.”

Becky looks at him blankly.

“Your appearance, you did what I asked.” He specifies for her.

“Oh, thanks,” she says with a coy smile.

Black scoots his chair back from the table. “Ready to leave?”

When he stands up, Becky notices how tall he is, over six feet. “Shouldn’t we ask for the bill?” She gapes up at him.

“We’ve paid. Come on.”

Becky gets up and follows Black out the door of Luciano’s and into his car in the parking lot, where he proceeds to drive them to their next destination.

She checks out the polished interior of Black’s Mercedes AMG Roadster. The unhurried guitar strum of an alternative song plays at a low volume.

She sits down in her desk chair, just relaxing for a moment. A tiny smile crosses her lips.

Becky stoops forward in her chair over the keyboard. She opens her email and begins typing a new message to Black.

“Something short and sweet seems appropriate for a non-date,” she says to herself. Right after she hits ‘send’, Becky second guesses herself. She clicks on her inbox. The mouse pointer hovers over Black’s reply to the Q&A email from earlier in the day. Becky opens the email and scrolls through it. She stops on a segment that resonates with something he said at the club that night.

Keep in mind that your role in this will always be changing. So if there’s a part you don’t really like, something different is around the corner.

She reaches over to open a desk drawer and fishes out a pad of paper. Becky sets the notepad down on her desk.

As long as you can take the bad with the good, you’ll eventually get to make rules instead of obey them.

Becky picks up a pen that’s sitting next to her keyboard. She hunches over the notepad. The tip of the pen hits the paper. Becky starts writing a list of everything she remembers from the day, including Express Courier Services, Ryan the driver, Restaurant–

She hesitates, unable to come up with the name of the restaurant, and switches gears. Becky opens an internet search window and types in ‘Express Courier Services California’. She combs through the first page of non-applicable results. Becky clicks on the second page of search results but finds nothing.

“How can it not exist?” Her forehead wrinkles with incomprehension. She taps the pen on the notepad and gets back to making her list, mumbling as she goes. “Club Joy, Geneva, Porsche guy...the twins.” Becky scowls.

***

Back at Club Joy, upbeat music fills the air. The V.I.P. balcony is still alive with activity. The blonde bartender is lining up shot glasses on the bar. Geneva and Trip are sitting in front of them.

Seated in one of the semi-circle booths are Cade, Black and three of his subs: Marsa, Minya and Kayleigh. The twins are snug up against Black. Next to Minya, Kayleigh sips on a daiquiri drink while Cade finishes sending a message. He sets his phone down on the table. Across the booth from Cade, Marsa rests her head back on the padded bench behind her. She aims her twinkling, diamond-polished nail at Black.

“I want you to collar me, so I can never leave you,” she says to him.

“What?” Black peers at her, obviously a little stunned to hear her say that. “You have had a lot to drink tonight, haven’t you?” He leans over and lightly kisses her forehead.

“No, that doesn’t matter.” Marsa beseeches.

Across the room, Random appears at the top of the spiral staircase. He browses the balcony level crowd before making his way to the bar.

“It has nothing to do with that.” Marsa insists to Black, who reaches for his rum and cola.

“Mm-hmm.” He takes a drink.

“Kids.” Cade remarks about the fickle yearns of people in their early twenties. Black nods at him while Marsa presses on.

“Other Tops do it.”

“And others don’t,” Black tells her.

“Hey.” Cade gets his attention. “Random’s here.”

“He is?” Black skims the nearby booths.

“Over there. Getting a drink.” Cade gestures to the balcony bar where Random is picking up a whiskey on the rocks. He backs away from the bar and sees Rayne passing by.

“Rayne.” Random catches up with her by the iron railing. She spins around to him.

“Hi.” Rayne greets him with a genial wave. “When did you get here?”

“Just now.” He swirls the ice around his glass. “So have you heard from Sam lately?”

She shakes her head. “Not for a few days, why?”

“I was just wondering.” He brushes it off and steps back.

“Hey, why?” Rayne pounces on him. “Is something going on?”

“Nothing bad,” he says, baring an obscure smile. “You’ll find out soon enough.”

“Will I, though?” She looks past Random at Geneva approaching. “Okay, if you say so.” Rayne finishes interrogating him when Geneva joins them.

“I wasn’t expecting to see you, tonight.” Geneva lightly touches Random’s arm.

“I wasn’t expecting to show up.” A rhythmic bass beat thumps through the club. “I spent the evening working out a scene with Shay. We got it done, so I decided to get out for a while.” Random sips his whiskey.

“The one you and I are doing?” Rayne asks him.

“That’s the one.”

“Big job?” Geneva postulates, given that at least Shay, Random and Rayne are all involved.

“Yes, it’s pretty comprehensive,” he elaborates, “plus we’re accommodating a plane flight.”

“I see.”

“How’s your night going?” Random asks Geneva. 

“Well, we met Black’s project earlier.” She spills to him, comfortably buzzed.

“Yeah? Any initial thoughts?”

“She was definitely nervous,” Geneva answers. “But also very curious.”

“I’m curious, myself.” Random gives her a parting nod and walks over to Black’s booth.

Seated on the end, Cade glances up at him and shifts over to make room. Six is kind of a squeeze in the semi-circle booth, but Random gets situated on the edge of the seat. He turns to Black, over between the twins.

“How’d it go?” He sets his whiskey down on the table.

“If I hear from Becky after tonight, I think it’s in the bag.”

“Why,” Random sways forward in interest, “what’d you do?”

“I had Reno help me out with a little event on the dance floor and then sent her home with him.” Black has a sip of his drink.

“Why? Are you trying to drive her off?”

“No,” Black sets his glass back down, “but I needed to spend some time with these two.” He reaches up to the twins, on either side of him, and strokes their shoulders.

“Yes, happy birthday.” Random acknowledges them. The twins smile sweetly at him. Minya resumes her chat with Kayleigh beside her. Marsa laces her arm through Black’s and tunes into his and Random’s discussion. “What’s your hunch?” he asks Black.

“My hunch, is that Becky will reconcile tonight in her mind and be ready for round two in a few days.”

“You don’t suffer from any lack of confidence, do you?” Random smiles at Black. It’s an earnest smile, in lieu of his usual sneer. Black notices it.

“Not about this.” He warily studies Random’s show of amity. “What’s with you tonight?”

“I’m in a good mood,” Random tells him. Black tips his head in consideration and asks,

“Oh, what’s that like?”

“It’s a refreshing change. You should try it.”

Before he can respond, Black’s phone vibrates in his pocket. “I’ll bet you that’s Becky.” He takes his phone out and unlocks the screen.

“No way.” Random discards Black’s assumption.

“I have learned a thing about her over the past two months, you know?” Black moves his drink, plants his elbow on the table and holds his phone out to Random. “She sent the message ten minutes ago.”

“What does it say?” Cade leans into the phone.

Random reads Becky’s email message out loud. “It says, ‘Thank you for the evening. Look forward to hearing from you’.” He doesn’t hide his awe. “Wow,” he says and sits back in his seat.

“She wants to play.” Cade follows up.

“Persistent and bored.” Black shoves his phone back into his pocket. He folds his arms in front of him and shrugs at Random. “They either come around, or they don’t.”

***

Chamber 7 in the basement of the Mercer Estate is dark and quiet. Hannah’s voice gores through the silence.

“You know Brian, I think you really need to get in touch, with something, before it just gets too late for you.”

“Agreed.” His husky response echoes in the darkness. The whoosh of a paddle cutting through the air precedes the smack.

***

Right on schedule, a shiny black limousine sits parked in the driveway of the Mercer Estate, in front of its multi-car garage. Late morning sun bounces off of the chrome trim and wheels.

Inside, Shay and Reno are sitting in back. The stylish interior is well lit by overhead and panel lighting. A large TV screen is mounted above a sleek minibar area. Reno has an open file folder in one hand and a cardboard box of airplane-sized alcohol bottles in his lap.

“Next.” Shay sticks out her hand to Reno. He pulls a whiskey bottle out of the box and gives it to her.

“This has to be the most extensive set of target photographs that I have ever seen.” He leans in towards Shay. “She knows to look for a limo, right?”

“Of course she does.” Shay punctures the neck of the plastic airplane bottle with a syringe, shooting in a dose of golden-green fluid.

“I mean, he’s got daytime shots, nighttime, hair up, hair down, every angle imaginable. The pictures take up more room than the game plan.” Reno flicks the scenario game plan, a couple sheets of paper on the right side of the file, double punched at the top and fastened to the inside of the folder. Meanwhile, a thick stack of photo collages is fastened on the left side. He flips through the photographs and asks, “Where are the x-rays? Fingerprints?”

“I know, he was excessive.” Shay places the little whiskey bottle in the bar compartment. A half dozen bottles are already lined up in the slot. “Wayne’s pretty green. Next, please.”

Reno hands her over another bottle.

“They’ve never actually met in person, so he’s accumulated a lot of pictures.” She explains.

“What, was it an online thing, I take it?”

“Yeah, just over a year.”

“Why wait a year to meet?” Reno glances up from the file at Shay, who’s pushing in the plunger on the syringe.

“They were both wrapping up divorces. I guess they wanted everything finalized before meeting in person.” Shay withdraws the needle and sets the airplane bottle down next to the others. She picks up a small glass bottle to reload the syringe. Shay pokes the needle into the bottle and draws back the plunger, filling the syringe with marijuana tincture.

“Yeah, especially if they went to court.”

“That’s what I gathered.” Shay taps the stem of the syringe with her fingernail.

“I have to say, I am very satisfied with the effect of the THC-laced alcohol.” Reno passes her another bottle. “It puts them out for just the right amount of time, and you don’t have to stress out about dosage.”

“I don’t know if I agree. I’ve had a couple times when the target came around too soon, and I still had to use the anesthetic.” Shay works the tip of the needle beneath the label on the little bottle and carefully stabs it into the plastic.

“Really? They probably didn’t get enough.” The targets do typically pass out before finishing their first drink. “I’ve had good luck with it.” He mentions to her. “Once they conk out, I’ve got a solid hour, if not more.”

“Well, regardless of the chemical, everybody reacts a little differently. Can you imagine trying to make Black pass out from a marijuana tincture?” Shay pulls the needle out of the bottle. “Maybe with an IV?”

“True, different tolerance levels.” Smiling, Reno closes the file and sets it down on the leather seat. Shay slips the bottle of gold tequila into the bar compartment. Reno digs into the box and holds out a clear vodka bottle. Shay looks at it, and then looks at the syringe of greenish fluid in her hand.

“I need the blue-colored vodka bottle.”

“Oh, right.” Reno chortles at his oversight.

“Smoke on your way down here this morning?”

“I did.” He drops the clear bottle back in the box and pulls out the blue one.

“Uh-huh.” Shay takes the bottle from Reno. “Thank you.” She proceeds to work the tip of the needle into the plastic.

“When do I need to pick her up at the airport, anyway?”

“Monday morning, bright and early.” Shay slowly depresses the plunger on the syringe.

“How early?”

“The plane lands at ten-fifteen. You should be there by ten, just to play it safe.”

“Really?” He groans. “It’s kind of a long drive down there.” Reno will have to be awake, dressed and ready to leave Mercer by 9:00 or so, which is rather early for him.

“The flight is the one thing we did not coordinate.” Shay carefully plucks the needle out of the bottle.

“It’s all right, that’s not too bad. It could be worse.”

***

Sunday afternoon, Black walks past a black shoji room divider shading the recreational half of Cade’s office in his suite at the Mercer Estate. The surge of an explosion bursts out of the room’s surround sound speaker system. Cade glances up at Black while punching the control buttons on the arms of his gaming chair.

“Well good afternoon.” Cade pauses the video game, freezing the battle image on the large screen across from him. Black slides into the matching gaming chair beside Cade. There’s an end table between the two chairs. A red acrylic bong sits on the table. “Welcome back to the land of the lazy.”

“Happy to be back.” Black sets a can of soda down on the table next to the bong. The shelves below the large screen house a ridiculous collection of video games and an extensive library of pornography. Cade has a physical media fetish.

“What took you so long?” Cade goads him.

“Honestly? If you think recruiting a sub is tough, try converting an overactive, ordinary mind into a Top.”

“No thanks.” Cade chuckles before defensively adding, “But this isn’t just any old sub recruit I’m planning, by the way.”

“Of course it isn’t.” Black retorts. “Your one-upmanship is astounding, by the way.”

“I’m not downplaying your pursuit whatsoever. I would never attempt to do what you’re doing.”

“Because you couldn’t.” He reaches over for his can of soda and cracks it open.

“Not too proud to admit that.” Cade professes to him. “I’m fully aware that there’s only one reason I’m here, and it’s that law degree hanging on the wall above my desk over there.” He motions over his shoulder at the wall behind them.

“Necessity versus asset.” Black gibes and takes a drink.

“More or less. Anyway no, I would never try and pull off what you’re doing.” He asks Black for an update. “Have you heard from her since Friday night?”

“No, I think Becky’s smart enough not to blow up my email all weekend. That would rapidly end the game.” Black turns his attention to the large screen across from him. “So are you gonna fire this back up?”

“Hang on.” Their conversation provokes Cade to check his own inbox. “Oh, here it is.” He seizes up at the sight of her reply.

“What?” Black slides his hands down the arms of the chair to the control buttons.

Cade opens the consent form on his screen. “I got the go-ahead.” He posted a comment to his target’s story a week ago before messaging her directly today through the website, making it clear he was a legit user of the site, then extended an invitation to play the game. “She agreed.”

***

That evening, Shay and Hannah converge in the penthouse corridor in front of the door to Hannah’s suite. The word ‘Heretic’ is mounted on her door in antiqued gold letters.

“So, I noticed you have a new one.” Shay shoots Hannah a congratulatory nod.

“Yes I do.” Hannah raves. “He’s totally on board.”

“Impressive. What’s his name, again?”

“Brian.”

“He’s cute.”

“Mm-hmm.” Hannah puckers her fleshy lips in agreement. “He is kind of, isn’t he? Not that it really matters, but yeah.”

“Never know when it might come in handy.” Shay pontificates.

“No, you don’t.” Hannah sees Reno waltzing up to them in the corridor.

“Is the plane still on schedule?” he asks Shay.

“Yes, so you still have to get up early tomorrow, I’m afraid.” She feigns sympathy while resting her shoulder on the doorframe of Hannah’s suite.

“I was just checking.” Reno snarls at Shay and continues down the hallway.

***

The gloss black limousine is parked right outside the revolving doors of the international airport amid a row of taxis, slow-moving cars and travelers passing by on foot. Dressed sharp in a black suit, Reno leans against the limousine. He casually shoves his hands into his pant pockets. Reno scans the people filing out of the revolving doors. He unmistakably spots the target, Jessie, who heads right for the limo. Jessie’s short black hair and tan skin match up perfectly with the array of pictures Reno saw. She’s in a white lightweight sweatshirt and khaki shorts.

Jessie approaches Reno, carrying a bag over her shoulder and pulling a suitcase behind her.

“Jessie?” Reno uses the key fob in his pocket to unlock the trunk.

“Yeah,” Jessie answers him brightly. He opens the back door for her.

“I’m Josh,” Reno says. “Go ahead and have a seat. Let me get those for you.” He takes the handles of Jessie’s luggage so she can climb into the limousine.

Once she gets settled into the backseat, Jessie inspects the posh interior. Everything from the inviting minibar setup in front of her, on up to the television screen is pristine. She notices the dividing window to the front seat is down.

Reno gets into the driver’s seat and pulls the door closed. He flips on the left turn signal and merges into the traffic exiting the airport terminal. Reno glances at Jessie in the rearview mirror.

“Wayne said this is your first time in California. First time meeting each other, actually.” Reno’s small talk is obviously much more information than Jessie expected him to know.

“Oh really, he told you that?”

“Sure, why not?”

“Do you two know each other?” she asks.

“Yeah.”

“Really?” Jessie huffs, stumped by this news.

“Yes, why do you sound so surprised?”

“Well.” After an awkward delay she says, “Wayne’s a doctor.”

Reno looks back at Jessie in the rearview mirror with a brusque smile. “Are you implying he wouldn’t associate himself with a limo driver?”

“Well no, I–” Jessie stammers, “I didn’t mean any offense.”

“I tell you what, Jessie. It’s a pretty long drive, so you may as well fix yourself a drink.” He recommends.

“That sounds like a good idea.” Blushing in embarrassment, Jessie rifles through the spiked bottles of alcohol. She selects the little bottle of dark rum.

“Tell me what kind of music you like. I’ll roll up the window and let you relax.”

“You don’t have to do that. I’m not as arrogant as I came off.” Jessie sets a glass down on the polished shelf in front of her.

“I’ve dealt with a lot worse, trust me.” Reno asserts.

Smiling, Jessie opens the mini fridge and finds an ice bucket inside. She uses the silver tongs to drop a few cubes into her glass. Jessie twists the cap off of the rum and pours it over the ice. She finds a small container of pineapple juice in the refrigerator. After giving it a shake, she fills the rest of her glass with the juice.

“I’m sure you have some crazy stories.” Jessie puts the pineapple juice back in the fridge.

“Most of my clients are professionals, actually.”

“Oh, okay. So you don’t have to deal with the horror of prom nights and wedding parties then, huh?” She picks up her glass.

“No, I mainly deal with arrogance.” Reno’s curt reminder of her earlier gaffe prompts Jessie to start sipping her drink.

This is what Reno was aiming for. He powers on the television in back for her to tune into and waits for the next stage of the game plan to unfold.

In less than ten minutes, Jessie is putting her empty glass into the nearest cup holder. She’s slumped down in the seat with lidded eyes. Quiet and placid, she stares at the television, blinking frequently to keep her eyes open. On the screen, a movie plays at a low volume.

“I cannot believe how bad the jetlag is hitting me. I am sooo tired,” Jessie says through a tranquil yawn.

“Take a short nap.” Reno waves over his shoulder at her. “I’ll wake you up when we get there.”

“Do I have time?” She murmurs, becoming more addled by the second. “I mean, is it worth it?”

“You’ve got a good half hour or more, depending on traffic. Go right ahead.”

“Yeah.” Jessie languidly repositions herself, lying down on the lengthy seat. “I think I need to sleep this off.”

“There’s a pillow in here.” Reno reaches through the window into the back and opens up a compartment door containing pillows and blankets.

“That is excellent.” With suppressed enthusiasm, Jessie pulls a pillow out of the compartment and slides it under her head. When Reno closes the compartment door, his phone begins to ring. Jessie hears it and asks, “Is that Wayne?” in a slurred voice.

“Nope, it’s for me. Get back to your nap.”

“Okay.”

Reno answers his phone. “Hello Shay.”

“How’s it going?”

“Fine. She’s hit the miasmic stage.”

“Miasmic?” Shay laughs. “You’ve been hanging around Black too much.”

“I don’t always have a choice.”

“He’s starting to rub off on you. Anyway, I was just checking in.”

“I’ll let you know when we get there.” Reno ends the call. He can hear Jessie’s slow, deep breaths in the backseat.

***

Meanwhile in the WPC courtyard area, Becky and Jackie are sitting at a shaded table having lunch. Becky picks at her chicken sandwich, stuck in a distracted fog. There’s been no word from Black, not even a response to the email she sent thanking him for Friday night. Becky is openly grasping the concept of ‘anticipation mode’.

“But I thought we should definitely go with the pens.” Across the table, Jackie is in the process of hashing out wedding details. “Don’t you think?”

Becky notices that Jackie’s not talking. She jumps back into the conversation. “I’m sorry Jackie, say that again.”

“For the groomsmen gift, wouldn’t you go with the engraved fountain pen sets?”

“Oh, yeah.” Becky takes a bite of her sandwich. She puts it down and reaches for her phone on the table to refresh her email inbox while Jackie babbles on about the debate surrounding the groomsmen gift.

“And after all that, we end up deciding on the pen sets anyway.” Jackie crooks her head. “In silver, of course.”

“Of course.” Increasingly restless, Becky sets her phone down and gets back to her chicken sandwich.

“So, the only other thing we actually got around to picking up this weekend, were the little...” Jackie’s story fades into the background as Becky zones off again. She hasn’t solved the mystery of the fake delivery van. The delivery driver had a fancy silver fountain pen, much like the pen Jackie was just talking about. Jackie’s voice reemerges into the foreground. “And I think they’ll come together great. Is everything okay, Becky?”

“Yeah,” Becky tells her. “It’s just a Monday thing, you know?”

“Oh!” Jackie sucks in a quick gasp. “That reminds me. Did you hear Brian was a no-show today?”

“No, I did not hear that,” Becky answers, quite surprised.

***

Chamber 3 in the Mercer Estate basement looks remarkably similar to a standard exam room. The nitrous tank in the corner seems a bit out of place, but aside from that, it’s pretty spot on. Framed human anatomy posters hang on the walls. Across from the door is a counter with a small stainless-steel sink and a cabinet down below. The shelves mounted above the sink hold an enema bag and a stack of paper dressing gowns.

The exam table sits in the center of the room. There’s an IV stand on one side of the table and an adjustable floor lamp on the other. Jessie is lying back on the exam table, fast asleep. Her feet are up in the stirrups.

Dressed in a paper gown, Jessie inhales sharply. She comes to just as Random cinches a leather belt around her right ankle. Jessie lifts her head and glimpses around. Her left ankle is already fastened to the stirrup of the exam table. Jessie instinctively tries to sit up, which is when she realizes that her arms are bound to the sides of the table, wrapped with coils of thick white nylon straps.

A shriek of anxiety escapes through Jessie’s mouth. Random feeds the end of the belt into its buckle and pulls it tight. He’s wearing a white jacket. A stethoscope hangs around his neck. Random looks down at Jessie.

“You’re awake. We can get started.”

chapters.title: Chapter 4
chapters.content:
Chapter 4

“Brian just didn’t show up today?” Outside in the WPC courtyard area, Becky ganders at Jackie across the picnic table. Her half-eaten chicken sandwich sits on the wrapper in front of her.

“Yeah, he didn’t call in or anything. And he’s even got his phone turned off.” Jackie fills her in on the juicy details.

“Really?”

“Uh-huh.” Jackie arches her thin brows. “I guess Gary doesn’t want to make any final decisions or anything yet. He’s giving him until tomorrow to call in.”

“Really?” Becky repeats, tilting her head. “That is so strange. It’s just not like him.”

“I know. As much of a drunk ass as Brian is, he always makes it to work.” Jackie pulls her phone out of her purse to check the time.

Becky continues rambling, stuck in an incredulous funk. “Plus, he’s like best friends with Rob. Why would he leave his phone off?”

“I don’t know, but I need to pop by the restroom on my way back in.” Jackie drops her phone back into her purse.

“What odd timing for Brian to fall off the radar.” Becky muses.

“How so?”

“Nothing, just in general.”

“I’m gonna get moving, then.” Jackie stands up from the table to head inside.

“Okay, I’ll talk to you later.” Becky watches her go and says to herself, “Am I losing my mind?”

“Do you want to lose your mind?” A random co-worker asks Becky in jest, on his way past her table.

“If I haven’t already.”

***

Back in chamber 3, Random leisurely walks over to the counter. Underneath the counter is a leather-upholstered rolling stool.

Jessie takes in her surroundings. Much to her absolute shock, everything about the exam room seems to be appropriate. Her glare darts from the blood pressure cuff hanging on the wall, to Random, who pulls out the rolling stool and has a seat.

“What is this?” she asks frantically. “What am I doing here?”

“You came into town to meet Wayne, correct?”

“Yeah.” Jessie’s eyes bulge.

“This is your first time meeting.” He acts very matter of fact. “You need to get checked out.”

“That’s crazy.” She shakes her head. “I don’t even know how I got here.” Jessie tries twisting her upper body, but there’s no give in the nylon straps binding her arms to the sides of the table.

“You passed out in the limousine on your way from the airport. We brought you in here on a stretcher.” Random turns to the counter beside him and opens a drawer.

“No. No, there’s no way I drank enough to pass out. Not like this.” Jessie tries to assess her situation.

Random pulls a pair of latex gloves out of the drawer. “Well, you would’ve wound up here either way.” He snaps on a glove. “Whether you’d have passed out or not.”

“Why? And why am I tied down? Why?” Jessie’s frustration escalates.

“Because you were unconscious.” Random calmly pulls on the other latex glove. “And I knew you’d be disoriented. I didn’t want you to fall off the table. Safety first.” He quips, rolling the stool in closer to her. The paper gown is draped down between Jessie’s open knees.

“No, this isn’t right.” She stresses, clenching her fists. “Where is Wayne? Is he here?”

“He is, but he asked me to do the exam.”

“I don’t... Are you even a real doctor?”

Highly insulted, Random says, “Of course I am,” in a way that extinguishes any doubt.

On the other side of the door to chamber 3, Rayne is dressed in a pair of light blue scrubs, waiting for her cue. She rests her hand on a stainless-steel cart. The tray on top of the cart holds a variety of medical instruments, including hemostats, a thermometer, gauze and a speculum.

Inside the chamber, Random turns to the metal door and calls out,

“Rayne!” He turns back to Jessie. “And he knows exactly where you are.”

The door opens, and Rayne backs into the chamber bringing the cart inside. After pushing the cart over to Random, Rayne closes the chamber door behind her.

Rayne’s arrival gives Jessie a spark of hope. “Please, help me.” She begs her.

“Help you what?” Rayne asks, genuinely bemused.

“Untie me, I’m awake now. I don’t need this.” Jessie wriggles her strapped arms and jerks her ankles. The belts dig into the tops of her bare feet.

“It’s just better this way,” Rayne tells her in a staid tone.

“It is?” She blurts back.

Random swivels his stool around to the stainless-steel cart beside him. “Believe me.” He looks over his shoulder at Jessie, flaunting a frank expression. “I’ve done this a lot.”

“Why didn’t Wayne tell me about this?”

Random picks up a tube of lubricant from the steel tray and places it onto the thick, blue paper towel alongside some swabs in sealed tubes. “Don’t be coy,” he says with an errant smile. “Think I don’t know why you’re in town?”

“Where is he?” Jessie asks, noticeably quieter.

“Maybe, eight feet away.” Random reveals.

On the wall above the counter is a large rectangular box with a metal frame. The opaque white film in the frame makes it appear to be an x-ray light box. It’s actually a viewing window for the observation booth on the other side of the wall...

Inside the chamber 3 observation booth, a laminated counter runs along the length of the small room. Speakers are mounted on the walls and LED strips along the floorboards light up the perimeter.

Jessie’s voice comes through the speakers, asking, “He’s eight feet away?”

Shay, Geneva and Wayne sit in desk chairs at the counter, supervising the exam room. Wayne is outright captivated by the scene playing out in the chamber. Shay nudges him and whispers,

“It’s almost time for you to go in.”

Wayne nods but stays fixed on Jessie...

On the other side of the observation booth window, Random is standing next to the exam table. “I’ve been telling you he’s right here.”

“Then he can hear me.” Jessie assumes.

“Yeah, he can hear you.” Random walks over to the nitrous tank in the corner. He picks up the mask and hands it over to Rayne, who encourages Jessie to make the most of the experience.

“He’ll hear you if you want to scream a little.” Rayne puts the mask on her.

“Got an idea of what’s happening now, Jessie?” Random pushes the power button on the nitrous machine. It expels a faint hum.

“I do.” She decompresses when Random twists the dial on the machine’s instrument panel. After all, Wayne’s contract didn’t specify who would be initiating the scene.

***

The guest rooms on the main floor of the Mercer Estate are designed exactly like any customary upscale hotel room. Contemporary canvas prints hang on the walls, and two tall, brushed aluminum lamps sit on the sleek dresser. The ivory sheers covering the windows filter the afternoon sun.

Relocated to the guest room, Jessie lies on the king-size bed with a white sheet wrapped around her naked body, peaceful and content. Waking up tied to the exam table in chamber 3 a few hours earlier seems to be a distant memory for her.

“You’re not too upset with me, are you?” Wayne asks from his chair by the window, behind Jessie in the background.
