“Here.” Hannah leans in towards him. “I bet you wish you could scratch that.” She gently runs her nails around Rob’s mouth and across his cheeks. “He said you’re a really good friend. One who would try and understand why he did what he did.”

“Is he coming back?” Rob sounds unnerved.

Hannah pulls her hand away from his face and eases back into the couch cushion. “Well, he never really left. So, in a sense, yes. But is he coming back here?” She holds up her hands and gestures around the apartment. “No.” Hannah relaxes her hands down into her lap. “And he won’t be back to work.”

“So how come?” Rob grows insistent. “I know he’s like a magnet to weird shit, but what exactly has he gotten himself into?”

“The alternative lifestyle, it’s what he was looking for.”

Rob listens but has a pessimistic scowl on his face.

“I know it might seem like I just,” Hannah shrugs, “snatched him from the strip club that night, but he was a completely willing participant from the get-go.”

“To the extent of walking out on his job of seven years, shutting off his phone and letting strangers pack up his apartment?” Rob’s inflection is dubious. “I know you know what I mean here, right?” He probes her.

“I do.” Hannah reassures him. “I completely understand how it must look. In fact, that’s why I’m talking to you first. Brian can tell you how he feels about all of this, and he will, but if you’re looking for intelligible answers, I have them.”

“How do you know how Brian feels better than him, when you just met him four days ago?”

“Because I’m more familiar with this process in general. I’ve gone through it with many other people.”

In the bedroom, Will is ripping the duct tape. Rob flinches at the sound.

“The basic reasons why people get into this lifestyle are similar.” Hannah explains. “I get why Brian wanted to leave with me that night. And he did know what he was getting into. We discussed it before we ever left the club.”

“And he knew, at that moment, that he’d be abandoning his whole life? I’m sorry, but I find that hard to believe.” Rob disputes her.

“That’s fine. He’ll tell you himself. In his own words, which, lack eloquence but may at the very least convince you that Brian’s actions are entirely of his own accord. And maybe that’s all you really need to understand at this point.”

***

It’s going on lunch hour and they don’t serve food, so there are only a handful of people in the small, neighborhood sports bar. Most of them are seated at the bar, watching one of several muted television screens hanging all over the walls.

Rob is at a cocktail table by himself. Anxiously waiting, he swirls the whiskey around in his glass. His phone is sitting in the middle of the table. Finally, it begins to ring. The call comes in as ‘unavailable’. Rob answers his phone on the first ring. “Hello?”

“Hey Rob, what’s up?” Brian’s carefree attitude comes through on the other line.

“What’s up?” Rob’s fingers grip down around his phone. He responds in a low, irate roar. “Your phone’s been off for the past four days. Two strange guys in your apartment jumped me and tied me up earlier today.” Highly sarcastic, he asks, “What’s up with you?”

“Yeah, sorry about that.”

“I am so freaked out that I actually waited in a public place for you to call, because I’m scared to go home.” Rob admits, guileless and sweaty.

“Oh no, don’t be. That’s ridiculous.”

“Is it?” His nervous eyes flit around the bar. “I’m not so sure. I don’t know what you got yourself mixed into, but these people are serious.”

“You do not have to worry about going home, okay.” Brian flat out tells him.

“What’s going on?” Rob throws his hand up in frustration. “What happened Friday night?”

“Listen, why don’t we just meet up at Tiger’s tomorrow night?”

Rob’s palm lands on the table in front of him, calmed down. “Okay.”

***

Becky opens the door to Exotica tattoo parlor and steps inside. Colorful decals partially cover the stucco walls of the parlor. Becky walks up to one of the black leather-bound books hanging from the ceiling on cable wires. She opens it up to check out the sample designs.

“Can I help you?”

“Yes.” Becky shuts the thick book. The employee, a bald white woman with a silver nose ring, is behind the beaded curtain in the doorway across from Becky. “I was wondering if I could go back there. I’m meeting somebody here.”

“Who?” The employee pulls the beaded curtain open.

Becky stalls. “Um, I really just need to take a look.”

“Okay. Have a look around, then.” She welcomes Becky in, parting the beaded curtain for her.

“Thank you.” Becky passes through the curtain. She stands at the end of a hallway of doors.

“Go ahead, the rooms are all open.”

Becky treks down the hallway and sheepishly peeks into each open door. When she checks the second door on her right, she catches a glimpse of a familiar face. Reno’s reclined back in a cushy black tattoo chair. His face is turned towards the door, but his eyes are closed. Becky dismisses the familiarity and continues down the hallway. She stops, suddenly disdained. Becky backs up to take a second look. It’s the Porsche guy.

Becky walks into the studio, where Reno is having work done on his smooth chest. The tattoo artist, Alice, is a twenty-something female whose long hair hangs in little braids. She has a barbell in her left eyebrow and chains tattooed up her arms. Alice lifts the machine from Reno’s skin when she sees Becky come in.

“Hello again.” Becky sits down on a wooden stool near the door. The smell of antiseptic drifts through Alice’s studio. Midday sun shines through the large window across from the door. Reno nonchalantly glances over at Becky.

“What are you doing here?”

“I was hoping you could tell me that.” She retorts.

The machine hums as Alice gets back to work on his tattoo.

“Make yourself comfortable, by the way. This here is Alice, since you didn’t bother asking.”

“Sorry, it’s nice to meet you...” Becky notices the chain tattoos running up Alice’s arms, “...Alice.”

Alice politely smiles but doesn’t look up from her work.

“What are you having done, there?” Becky asks Reno.

“You read, right?”

“Yeah I can read.” Ruffled by his brashness, she hops off the stool and leans over the black outline on Reno’s chest. “Travesty?”

“See the little badges Alice is putting inside of the letters?”

“I see them.” Becky sits back down on the stool. “I don’t see the significance.”

“How would you?” he asks.

“I don’t know. Are you gonna tell me?”

“I used to work Nevada. This is my insignia. We all have one.”

“Okay.” Becky wonders out loud. “So, what’s Black’s insignia, then?”

“Oh, it’s–” Alice goes to answer, but Reno interjects.

“He can tell you himself. Sorry Alice, I didn’t mean to cut you off.”

“No problem.”

“Oh, now just a minute.” Becky stares at Alice in astonishment. “You’re in on it, too? Am I the only one in town that isn’t aware of this?”

A thin laugh trickles out of Alice’s mouth. She puts down her machine and picks up a white towel. She wipes Reno’s chest with the towel while he reaches for his pack of cigarettes sitting on the barstool next to him. He lights one up.

“What exactly do you want to know, Becky?” Reno tosses down the lighter and exhales a cloud of smoke.

“Anything I want to know?”

“How about this, as long as you don’t waste my time with stupid questions, I’ll grant you three answers.” He proposes. “But only three, so give it some thought.”

Alice gets up from her stool to fetch an ashtray for Reno. She sets it on the barstool next to his pack and busies herself during Reno’s cigarette break.

“All right.” Becky gets down to business. “Is there some sort of name for this society you all belong to?”

“Not really, but if you’re involved, you’re a party member and if you live on site, you’re the inner party. Get it?” Reno’s 1984 reference sails right over Becky’s head. She foolishly rushes to her second question.

“Black’s in the inner party, then?”

Reno grimaces at her. “Are you sure you want to waste your second question like that?”

“No, actually I don’t, thank you.”

“Black this, Black that. You don’t even know my name, do you?”

Becky doesn’t respond. She rests her elbows on her knees diffidently.

“But you’re not wasting your second question on that nonsense, are you?” Reno sneers at her, flicking his cigarette into the ashtray. “Do you have any tattoos, Beck?”

“No, I don’t. I’m a chicken when it comes to needles.” She admits.

“Is that right? Did you know that the biggest pussies are the ones who most enjoy inflicting pain?”

“Is that a fact?”

“That it is. Pain’s never been my thing.” He pauses to take a drag of his cigarette. “Let’s hear question number two.”

“I’d like to know if there’s a point to my visit here, today.”

Smoke swirls out the corners of Reno’s mouth as it curls downward in disappointment. “That is a poorly thought out question. Weren’t you told to come here to redeem yourself? You already know the point, Becky.”

“Oh, come on.” She coaxes him. “It was just bad phrasing.”

“No way, I’m not letting you slide twice in a row. Make number three count.”

Becky glowers at Reno. “Well, I don’t really have a choice. I have to know what I’m supposed to do to redeem myself.”

Reno sits up straight and turns sideways on the chair. He fishes the phone out of his jeans pocket. “Here, this is for you.” He bends forward, handing the phone over to Becky.

“A phone?” She takes it from him.

“It’s yours, but you can only use it to communicate with Black.” Reno lies back in the black vinyl chair. “You have no way of finding out the number to the phone. But try all you want.”

“Okay, let’s see here.” The phone chimes when Becky powers it on. A bewildered frown comes over her face. “What the hell is ‘random’? What kind of phone service is that?”

Reno rolls his eyes towards Alice and says, “A very private one.” He snuffs out his cigarette. Alice laughs quietly in the background. She picks up her machine and goes back to work on Reno’s tattoo.

“I’ve never heard of such a thing.”

“Anyway, if you redeem yourself, you keep the phone. But your act of atonement is entirely optional.”

Becky lowers the phone. “It’s optional?”

“Optional is a choice– that you either make or you don’t.” He informs her.

“Yes, thank you. But how does it apply in this situation?”

The tattoo machine hums while Reno elaborates. “You have to choose whether to move forward in the game, or get out of it.”

“You mean quit?”

“Right.”

“So, it’s really not optional.”

“It’s definitely optional. No one can force you to get a clit ring.”

Becky blasts out an appalled huff. “No, that’s what he expects me to do?” She crosses her arms over her lap.

“That’s right.”

She bats her eyes in disbelief. “That’s insane.”

“Once again, it’s entirely optional.” He reminds her.

Becky throws her head back, still clinging to the phone. “I’m on my lunch break right now.” She frets.

“And?”

“And this is a pretty major decision to make over my lunch hour.”

“Is it? Piercings aren’t permanent.”

She crosses her arms back over her lap. “You have a point.” Her frustration subsides. Becky bounces her foot in deliberation.

“It’s ironic, isn’t it? That your act of atonement for being impulsive, is being asked to do something impulsive.” Reno marvels at his own cleverness and then resumes his relaxed mode.

“Just not on my terms.”

“Of course not.” He hacks and then comments to Alice. “Somebody here really needs to get with the program.”

“In all seriousness, is this worth it?” Becky candidly asks Reno.

“If I were you, I’d go ahead and do it.”

“Would you? Get a clit ring, really?”

“I said ‘if I were you’.” Reno glances at Alice. “She’s a mouthy one, isn’t she?”

“A little, yeah.” Alice limits herself to answering direct questions from Reno.

“Of course it’s worth it,” he tells Becky and asks Alice, “wouldn’t you agree?”

“I agree completely,” Alice says, absorbed in her work.

“See, I wouldn’t lie to you, Beck.”

“Right, so let’s say I do this.” She hypothesizes. “How would I let him know?”

“Remember that phone I gave you?”

Becky looks down at the phone. “The one in my hand, you mean? Yeah.” She opens the contacts on the phone, but the list is empty.

“It has a camera.”

“But I don’t have any phone numbers in here. How would I send it to him?”

“You don’t need to do a thing. He’ll get the picture.” Reno promises and spots Becky’s gaze of consideration.

***

Doleful alternative music drones on softly through Black’s office. He’s in his desk chair, staring at his laptop. He reaches for a coffee mug while scrolling down the page. Black’s phone buzzes on the desk beside him. He picks it up and opens the message. A camera image pops up on the screen. He lifts his brows in surprise when he sees the picture.

“Really Becky?” Black nods. “The game goes on, then.” He shuts off the display and sets down his phone. There’s a knock on the office door.

“Hey, you in there?” Cade asks from the other side of the door.

“Yeah, come in.” Black turns his chair around as the door opens. Cade walks in carrying a manila file folder. He hands it to Black and sits on a tall barstool across from him.

“There’s your copy.” Cade signals to the folder. On the tab, a name is written in black marker: Jane Bostick.

“The Jane Bostick abduction.” Black opens the folder and skims Cade’s game plan. “So you’re really going through with it?”

“Why not?”

“Why not.” Black repeats, still on the first page of the game plan. “I see that you assigned your best men to the job.” He mentions to Cade in a wry tone.

“Hey, take it as a compliment.”

“Why? Because you’re throwing caution to the wind and dragging me into it with you? That’s a compliment?”

“Yes. With you three, I don’t see what can go wrong.” Cade rests his elbow on the pub table beside him.

Black waves the game plan at him. “Have you talked to Random yet? Is he gonna be up for this?”

“I’ve talked to Random.” He apprises him.

“Really?” Black frowns, vaguely offended. “You gave him the plan before me?”

“I kind of needed him to know I was doing a high-risk scenario, and that I was expecting him to help me.” Cade laughs. “You know? I mean, he was gonna be the hardest one to convince.”

“What about Reno?”

“I’m meeting up with him as soon as he gets back here,” Cade answers. Reno will be the easiest one to get on board.

“Hmm.” Black gets through the first page and flips the sheet overtop of the folder. He continues reading. “It’s very detailed.”

“Take your time. Read it over.”

“Oh.” Black lowers the file, reaching back to pick up his phone. “Becky took the challenge, today.” He opens the picture from Becky and holds out his phone. Cade stoops down to check it out.

“So I see.” He pats Black’s chair. “That’s good news.” Cade sits back in his barstool. “What’s your next move?”

“I’m gonna stop over and see her tonight.” Black sets his phone back down on the counter behind him. Cade pulls his own phone out of his pocket and reads the message from Reno, saying he’s almost back to the house. He stands up from the barstool. On his way out, he asks Black,

“Have you figured out why Random’s so interested in her?”

“Not yet.”

“Hmm.” He leaves Black’s office and cuts through his living room to the penthouse corridor. Magenta’s vacuuming the corridor, but there’s no one else around. Cade travels down to his own suite at the west end of the hall. He walks into his office, leaves the door open and waits for Reno.

Seated at his desk in front of the bay window, Cade’s soft brown eyes sweep up from his laptop monitor to his office door. Reno strolls in and plops down on the leather chair across the desk from Cade. He sets a glass ashtray down on the corner of the mahogany desk.

“How far did Alice get on your tat?” Cade asks him.

“It’s coming along. I’m going back on Sunday.” He raises a cigarette up to his mouth. “Oh, guess what, Black’s little brat got a clit ring today.” Grinning, Reno lights the cigarette.

“Yeah, I saw it.” Cade slides a manila file folder across the desk to Reno.

“Ah yes.” He picks up the file and opens it.

“You’re playing the lure.”

“I’m not surprised.” Reno’s success rate relies on human nature’s innate trust for attractive people. He ashes his cigarette and then lounges back slowly into the chair. He delves deeper into the file contents. “Wait a minute, Jane Bostick? Is she any relation to–”

“Yes.” Cade interrupts him, chortling. “That’s why I’m being so careful. I can’t afford any risks.”

Reno glances at him. “I get it. Okay, then.” He redirects his focus back down to the game plan. “Where in the world did you find her?”

“Just on a website.” Cade brushes Reno off, reluctant to reveal too many personal details about Jane.

“Go on.” Reno blatantly ignores Cade’s attempt at discretion.

“It was an amateur story site.”

“Interesting.” He sets his cigarette in the ashtray and asks Cade, “What did she write about?”

Cade rests his head on the back of his chair. “Exactly what we specialize in around here.” He divulges.

“So,” Reno perks up with intrigue, “the proverbial black sheep. She’ll be a piece of cake.” He shoots Cade a smile of approval.

Across the desk, Cade’s computer dings with an incoming message. He bows in to read it. “Hmm, Trip’s bored on the plane.”

“What?” Reno cocks his head, wholly clueless. “Trip’s on a plane?”

***

In Black’s master bedroom, the dark brown drapes are pulled back, letting in the golden glow of early evening sun. A sitcom plays on the TV mounted above his stone fireplace.

Black walks out of the steamy master bathroom toweling off his damp hair. He’s dressed in olive pants and a black t-shirt, getting ready to leave for Becky’s. He throws his towel through the bathroom doorway onto the tile floor. His phone rings, so he goes over to the nightstand. Looking down at the screen with a smile, Black holds his phone up to his ear. “Well hello, Sam in Amsterdam.” He sits on the edge of his bed...

Sam’s living room is warmly lit by a candle on the coffee table and a kitsch floor lamp in the corner. It’s after 2:00 in the morning, and she’s just getting home from work. Sam sits down on her couch in a full length, faux leather jacket.

“Hello yourself,” she says to her phone, which is sitting on the coffee table on speaker with Black. Sam strips off her jacket to reveal the dominatrix gear she’s wearing underneath. She’s in a black vinyl halter top, laced up the front, with a matching miniskirt and arm gauntlets.

“To what do I owe the pleasure?” he asks.

“I have some news. But first, how are you?”

“I’m fine.”

“Your bullet-dodging days are behind you, then?” Sam props her right foot up on the edge of the coffee table and begins unlacing her knee-high boot.

“For the time being.”

“I’m glad to hear that.”

“What’s your news, Sam?”

“I’m moving back.”

Her statement silences Black. He connects the dots between Sam’s return and Random’s recent behavior. “Random...” he says under his breath, so quiet that she asks,

“What?” Sam blinks at her phone in confusion, unaware of the realization Black is coming to on the other line.

“Have you told Random?” His mood takes a feisty turn. “He must be excited.”

“Yeah, and so am I.”

“Not more than me.” Black’s reply carries a ring of insinuation.

Sam slips the boot off of her right foot and tosses it on the floor. “Hmm, that sounds sinister.” She starts on the laces of her left boot.

“Maybe it is.” He responds plainly.

chapters.content:
Chapter 5

Sam unlaces her left boot, tilting her head at the odd turn that her phone conversation with Black has taken.

“So when will you be back in town?” he asks her, resuming normal dialogue.

“It’s a few weeks off, yet.” Sam pulls off her left boot and sets it down next to its match on the floor. “But keep it to yourself for right now, okay?”

“Sure.”

“I just don’t know exactly when I’ll have everything wrapped up here.”

“What brought on the decision to come back?”

“Several things.” She smiles. “Why, do you want me to rethink it?”

“Of course not, I was just curious to what triggered it.”

“It’s a lot of things.” Sam reaches up and pulls the ponytail out of her long hair. “It just feels like the right time.” She shakes her head, causing thick curls to tumble over her shoulders.

“I see.” He lets her ambiguous answer slide.

“Do you have any interesting projects going on?”

“Yeah, funny you should ask. Random’s been really eager to help me out with it.”

Sam notes his implication. “And you think that’s because of me?”

“I know it is. This project is the exact type of thing he’d want me to be preoccupied with in the wake of your impending return.”

“Why?” She pivots towards her phone on the coffee table in sheer suspense. “What kind of project is it?”

“Turning an outsider into a Top.”

“Nice, that’s ambitious!” she says encouragingly. “How’s it going?” Sam begins unlacing her forearm gauntlets.

“Not bad. It’s still too soon to tell for sure, though.”

“It’s not an easy task.”

“So you’ve told me.” He alludes.

“Well, I’m interested to see how that goes for you.”

“As is the good doctor.”

Sam squints at his remark and then changes the subject. “What else is going on around there that I should know about, aside from the obvious?”

“Vienna’s moving,” Black tells her.

“I know.” She hisses. “I am so pissed off. Does she know when, yet?” Sam peels the gauntlet off her left arm and lays it down on the coffee table. She starts working on the laces of her right arm gauntlet.

“Not for sure.” He then changes the subject, himself. “I see you haven’t lost your knack for skirting the issue.”

“Black, I can’t weigh in on what Random’s thinking. How would I know? Maybe he just wants to be on good terms with you since I’m coming back.”

“No, he wants me to be busy. It’s pretty obvious now. But I really don’t expect you to weigh in.”

“You keep bringing it up, though.” Sam tosses the gauntlet down on top of the other one.

“Well, because I’ve been trying to figure this out, and I just got struck with the answer. You know how that is, when it all comes together in your head.”

Sam closes her eyes and softly laughs. “No, I don’t. That’s why I’ve been here for the past two years.”

“You’ll figure it all out when you get back.” Black assures her with an impious undertone.

***

Back in Cade’s office, Reno is still seated across the desk from him, holding the open Jane Bostick file. “Why is Trip on a plane?” he asks.

Cade looks at the clock in the corner of his computer screen. It’s 6:00 p.m. “I gotta go.”

“Where?”

With sudden urgency, Cade closes his laptop and stands up from his desk chair. “Over to the apartment.”

“Pedophile trapping?”

“Yup.” Cade reaches down to open a desk drawer. He takes out a 9mm gun and pushes the drawer closed.

“Have a good time.”

“I always do.” Cade leaves the office, gun in hand.

Closing the Jane Bostick file, Reno stays behind in the leather chair. He pulls out his phone and dials Shay.

“Hey Reno,” she answers.

“Hey. So, tell me why Trip’s on a plane.”

***

Trip is in the first-class section of the airplane cabin. The seat next to him is unoccupied. His overhead light shines down onto the laptop on his tray table. He leans forward, types a couple lines and relaxes back in his seat. Trip has a headset on.

Cade’s voice comes through the earpiece. “I didn’t think I’d make it here in time.”

“He should be there any second.” Trip talks quietly into the mouthpiece of his headset, concentrating on the laptop screen.

On the monitor, there’s a window with a live feed of Cade in a virtually empty apartment living room. He’s seated in an armchair with a briefcase in his lap. Cade glances up at the camera that’s mounted in the corner of the ceiling. “What profile did you use, by the way?” Cade opens the briefcase. A laptop computer is sitting on the table beside his chair. He takes a small speaker out of the briefcase and plugs it into the laptop.

“I’m BratMandy today,” Trip tells him.

“Okay. This is such an excellent waste of time.” Cade removes the 9mm gun from the briefcase and sets it on the table next to the laptop.

“It’s a community service, really.”

“Sure it is, and an entertaining one.” Cade reaches back into the briefcase for a pair of handcuffs. After slipping the cuffs into his pant pocket, he closes the briefcase and sets it down on the floor next to his chair.

“The drunk guy who shit himself.” Trip reminisces, quelling his laughter.

“Yeah, that was good.”

There’s a knock on the apartment door. Cade picks up the gun.

“Oh, here we go.” Glued to the screen, Trip watches the trap he set unfold...

Cade turns to the laptop. He starts up the first audio file he has in queue. A girl’s voice plays through the high-definition speaker.

“David?” The young voice is crisp and clear.

“Yeah, it’s me,” David says outside the door.

Cade plays the second audio file.

“Come on in, it’s open.”

Then he stands up from the chair.

The apartment door opens. Cade steps behind the door, and the middle-aged pedophile, David, walks inside. Cade pushes the door shut behind him and holds the gun to his head.

David freezes.

“Mandy had a change of heart.” Cade notifies him.

“Yeah, I’m figuring that out.”

Standing directly behind David, Cade presses the gun to his temple with a steady hand while taking the handcuffs out of his pocket. “Put your hands behind your back.”

David doesn’t resist. He slowly moves his arms behind him.

“Thirteen-year-old girls can be fickle, you know?” One-handed, Cade puts the pair of cuffs on David’s wrists. “In the meantime, we’ve learned all about you, David Alan Garrett. Everything. And that’s just to make sure you don’t ever try this sick shit again. You are officially on our radar. Understood?”

“Yes, it’s understood. I had a bad feeling.” David maintains a compliant and calm front.

“And yet here you are, despite it.” Cade walks away from him. He sets the gun down on the table next to the laptop.

“Am I getting arrested, then?” David asks.

“No, but for wasting our time, I need you to take your wallet out.” Cade has a seat in the armchair. He rests his hand on the gun. “How much cash do you have in there?”

“Not much, maybe like thirty bucks.” David gets his wallet out of his back pocket.

“That’s fine. Throw me your wallet. You’ve got credit cards, right?” Cade holds his hand out.

David sighs. “Are you taking everything?” He turns and tosses his wallet over to Cade.

“Nope.” Cade catches the wallet and flips it open. “I’m just collecting a few thousand towards rent and expenses. You can’t really expect us to foot the bills for this place, can you?” Cade shrugs, taking a couple of credit cards out of David’s wallet. He sets them down on his knee. Leaving one hand on the gun, Cade picks up his phone and starts typing a credit card number on the keypad.

“So a few grand, and that’s it? That’s what you want?”

Cade stops typing to say, “I could always kick your ass.”

***

Sitting at a stoplight behind the wheel of his Mercedes, Black turns off his stereo. Over on the passenger seat, his phone is ringing. He puts the phone on speaker. “Hello Random.”

“Hey, where’d you go?” Random asks on the other line.

“I’m stopping over to visit Becky.”

“Right, the newly pierced conquest. That really surprised me, I’ve got to admit.”

“She’s full of surprises. Anyway, I’ll be back in a little while. I’m sure Cade wants to get together and go over his game plan.”

“Actually, he’s out pedophile trapping right now.”

“Really?” Black’s forehead crinkles with interest.

“Yes. The reason I called you was to see if any of your girls want to bartend, the twins maybe?”

The light turns green. Black shifts into first gear and continues down the road lit up by streetlights. “They help out in the bar on Saturdays already, but I can ask them. Why?”

“Ryan wants to move across the hall for good,” Random tells him.

“Oh okay, I’ll keep that in mind.”

“Well enjoy your visit. I’m sure we’ll hear from Cade later.”

“Yeah, I’m sure we will.” Black reaches over to end the call. He turns into Becky’s neighborhood, drives past the row of townhomes and pulls into her driveway. Shutting off the engine, he walks up her front steps and rings the doorbell.

Becky opens the door and sees Black standing on her porch. She inspects his black t-shirt, Harrington jacket and olive pants. He looks put-together, even in basics. “Come in.” Becky backs up, and Black enters her living room. She closes the door behind him. “Do you want a mojito?” she asks him.

Black wanders in and stops, somewhat bemused by her drink offering. “You have everything on hand for a mojito?”

“I do,” Becky answers on her way to the kitchen. “I worked behind the bar at a Mexican restaurant when I was in college.”

Black’s brows arch upon learning Becky knows how to bartend. “Hmm, good to know.”

“What’s that?”

The lights are off in Hannah’s master bathroom that night. She hovers over her pale-colored granite vanity, lighting pillar candles with a stick lighter. Behind her, the bathtub fills with water. The milieu is somber. Hannah turns to her tub. Bundled in a fluffy white robe, she selects a bottle of almond milk bubble bath and squeezes it into the bathwater. The running water masks her sigh.

She reaches for her phone on the vanity and sets it on an empty soap dish in the tub before getting in there herself. Bubbles rise tall inside the deep tub while Hannah sheds her fluffy robe. She slips down into the water, immersing herself in the wall of white suds.

Hannah pokes her arm up out of the bubbles. She aims a finger down at her phone on the soap dish in front of her. She taps the screen a few times, picks up her phone and settles back into the chin-high suds. With her phone to her ear, she waits for Sam to answer...

Morning sun cheerfully lights up the living room of Sam’s Amsterdam flat. She is seated on her couch with her laptop. Her feet are propped up on the coffee table. A vase of blush peonies in the middle of her coffee table permeates the room with their sweet fragrance. Lying beside the vase, her phone rings with Hannah’s call.

Sam leans forward to answer, putting the call on speaker. “Hello?”

“Sorry Sam, it’s still real early there, isn’t it?” Hannah’s downbeat voice comes through on the phone.

“That’s okay, I’m up. Are you on the website?” Glancing down at her laptop screen, Sam guesses at the reason for Hannah’s call. Her long hair is pulled back in a ponytail. She’s wearing plaid pajama pants and a Pixies t-shirt.

“No, I just want to talk, if you have a minute.”

“To me?” Sam sounds befuddled.

“Sorry.”

“No, you’re fine.” She snickers at Hannah’s response. “It’s just not an everyday thing.”

“I know. And I hate to bother you, but Black’s out for the night, Cade’s in his own world right now, Will is part of the problem and Reno just pisses me off.”

“So, nobody else to talk to, huh?” Sam deduces.

“No offense.”

“None taken, what’s up?” She moves her laptop over to the couch cushion.

“I’m just a ball of nerves tonight, over a sub.”

Sam is stunned silent for a moment. “I don’t think I’ve ever heard you say those words before.”

“I’m not sure I have.”

“What’s gotten into you?” She hears Hannah blow a raspberry before laying it out for her.

“When something seems too good to be true, or comes too easily, I just wait for the other shoe to drop. And I don’t have this problem very often. Normally I work my butt off for everything, so it’s rare that I feel this way.”

“What’s the worst that could happen?” Sam asks her.

“I lose my investment in a new sub. Granted, he’s a very new sub, so there’s not a lot invested. But he just fell right into my lap when I really needed one, and he could be such a good fit in my suite.”

“Why do you think the other shoe’s gonna drop?”

“Because he agreed to meet up with like, his best friend, tonight.”

***

At that same time in Tiger’s lounge, Brian and Rob are at a high table near the bar. There are a couple pool tables around them, one of which is being used. Tiger’s lounge is homey and not very crowded. A round of laughter bellows out from the bar, over top of the trendy pop music playing.

“I never would’ve saw this coming.” Brian picks up his bottle of beer. “I didn’t even realize I needed a change, until I stepped out of my routine and really looked at it.” He sips his beer.

“What made you think you needed this big of a change, though?”

“It was time to break the cycle.” Brian explains his odd circumstances to Rob. “And not, not just with Becky. I was really falling out of touch.” He takes another swig of his beer and sets down the bottle.

“Falling out of touch with what?”

“Everything,” Brian answers genuinely. The crack of a pool ball being struck is heard in the background.

Wary-eyed, Rob has a partially drank whiskey and cola sitting on a coaster in front of him. “It didn’t seem that way to me.”

“I guess I was getting pretty good at playing the role.”

Rob slumps back in his chair. “I don’t know, man.”

“I was on autopilot constantly. The life I was living was just a way to ignore everything I was unhappy with.”

“Like what?”

“Like,” Brian chuckles, “normal life.”

“Come on.” Rob spouts, unamused by Brian’s vagueness.

“Seriously. Boring job, tiny apartment, bad relationships. Everything.” Brian’s reasoning doesn’t exactly appease Rob, whose forehead creases in concern.

“It really sounds like somebody put this idea into your head.” He reaches for his drink.

“No.” Brian zealously contests. “Nobody put any ideas in my head.”

“It sure seems that way.” Rob sips his drink.

***

“Anyway, this friend of Brian’s doesn’t think too highly of me, thanks to Will.” Hannah tells Sam while dragging her index finger through the top layer of frothy bubbles.

“Thanks to Will?” Sam’s puzzled question blasts out of Hannah’s phone.

“Yes, there was an ordeal.” She pokes her fingernail into the bubbles, popping them as she goes. “I mean, I don’t blame the friend for being a little turned off. I just hope he doesn’t talk Brian out of anything. It’s just so early on, you know?”

“Hmm, is Brian aware of the ‘ordeal’ involving the friend?”

“Yes.” Hannah pulls her finger up out of the bubbles and places her hand over her hairline, overly dramatic.

“If he already knows about it, then what’s the worry? Brian wasn’t a part of the situation, was he?”

“No, he was here, fortunately.”

“I think your bases are probably covered, then.”

“They probably are.” Hannah holds her foamy hand out. “But I don’t know. Part of me is just expecting him not to come back tonight.” She flicks the bubbles off her fingers.

“What could Will have possibly done to freak this guy out so bad?”

“Oh.” Hannah sighs.

***

“Okay, explain to me what happened at your apartment yesterday.” Back at Tiger’s, Rob’s elbows are on the table. He leans in towards Brian as though he’s trying to draw some sense out of him. “Because you kinda just blew that off.”

Brian’s enthusiasm dwindles in his effort to reconcile the apartment mishap. “I didn’t mean to blow it off. It’s just, the situation wasn’t as critical as you made it out to be.”

With a short and skeptical grunt, Rob sways back in his seat. “What version of the story did you get? Because it was a pretty big deal. I just went over there as a concerned friend.”

“I know.” Brian slides his empty beer bottle to the edge of the table.

“I heard a loud noise, so I went inside. And this very intimidating guy kicked the door shut, tied me up with a television cord and pinned me to the ground while another guy duct taped my mouth shut.”

A college-aged female bartender arrives at their table carrying another round of drinks. She cordially sets Rob’s whiskey and cola down on the table in front of him.

“Thanks Lisa.” Brian nods at the bartender and takes the fresh beer from her hand. She collects their empties and heads back behind the bar.

Rob lowers his voice. “How is that not a critical situation, Brian? Tell me.”

“Well...”

***

“Well?” With her phone held up to her ear, Hannah waits on pins and needles for a slice of Sam’s insight. The wall of bubbles has begun to collapse down around her shoulders. “I’m up against years of history, here.”

“Is Brian happy?”

“He sure seems to be.”

“So he knows what goes on there, and he knows what you’ll be expecting from him?”

“Yes, he’s moved in.” Hannah reminds her.

“What was his driving force, to let you recruit him in the first place?”

“Dissatisfaction. He’d grown fearless, cocky and borderline self-destructive, which led him to the dead end of monotony in his life. He thought he knew what was behind every corner until he met me and allowed me to re-instill fear into him.”

“The variability of fear ended the monotony.”

“And it brought him satisfaction. That was his driving force.” Hannah lifts her arm out of the bathwater. It’s coated in almond-scented bubbles.

“Makes sense.” Sam surmises.

“Yes, me explaining it to him made sense too, and me explaining it to you obviously makes sense.” She rests her elbow on the edge of the tub. “The question is, can he explain it to the outside world in a way that makes sense? Not only does he lack self-awareness, but he’s a MAN, Sam.” Hannah massages her temple.

“I understand that obstacle.”

“Then you understand why I’m panicking.”

“If he’s happy, and if he has found satisfaction, then he’ll find a way to explain it. History aside, I really think you’re worrying about nothing. I think you’re fine.”

“You’re probably right. It just seems too soon for him to face reality, to be back in normal life.”

***

When she sees the headlights of Black’s car turning into her driveway, Becky comes out the front door and pulls it closed behind her. She jogs down her front steps towards the Mercedes Roadster as Black gets out of it.

“Wow, and it’s even you picking me up,” she says in a blithe tone.

“Yes, I told you I’d give you the normal-life date you want.” Black walks over to open the passenger side door for Becky. He notices her off-the-shoulder white top and sprightly mood.

Becky gets into the car and flutters her lashes at Black. “So that means you have to tell me the truth, right?”

With his hand on the door, Black peers down at her. “I always tell you the truth anyway. You just don’t ask good questions.” He shuts the passenger door and gets in behind the wheel.

Becky watches him put the car in reverse, let up on the clutch and back out of her driveway. A raw, bluesy rock song by The White Stripes plays on his stereo. The streetlights along the road out of her neighborhood sporadically light Black’s calm profile inside the shadowy car.

“Where are we going?” She studies him up and down, from his profile to his hand pulling the stick shift into second gear.

“We’re just going for a drive. If there’s somewhere you want to stop, let me know.”

“Okay.”

He defers to Becky. “If that’s all right with you?”

“Yes, that’s fine.” She marvels at his change in demeanor. “Thank you for asking.”

“Don’t get used to it.” Black slows down at the stop sign at the end of her block and waits for the oncoming traffic.

Becky smiles, perusing around the inside of his car. She sees the silver mp3 player that’s plugged into a port in his center console. “Can I snoop through your music?”

“Yeah, go ahead.” Black turns right, heading out of the neighborhood.

“You don’t keep songs on your phone?” Becky picks up the mp3 player.

“I never have.”

“Hmm,” she pores over his music library and remarks, “you have got some unusual songs.”

***

Meanwhile at Tiger’s lounge, a droll nineties tune churns out of the digital jukebox by the front door.

“I know the apartment thing. I know it was all very strange.” Brian holds up his hand in acknowledgment.

“Not strange, scary.” Rob retorts.

“Okay, scary. But it wasn’t a threat to you, Rob. It was just a poorly handled situation.” Brian ensures him. “Still a bad thing, but that’s really all it was.”

“So you are blowing it off.”

Brian throws his head back in exasperation. Stuck in somewhat of a stalemate with Rob, Brian’s attention wanders over to the front door where a couple of people are entering the lounge. He sees a familiar face and raises his hand in a brief, friendly wave then gets back to Rob across the table. “Listen, I’m not blowing anything off, okay? They made a bad call. They shouldn’t have done that to you.” Sincere, he adds, “And I’m sorry it happened. I really am.”

Though Rob acts placated by his apology, he still can’t seem to get past this sudden transformation in Brian. “I can’t even believe we’re having a conversation like this.”

“It’s definitely weird.” Brian agrees. “But at least it’s different.” He takes a drink of his beer.

“This just doesn’t sound like you. Are you doing all this because you wanted to nail that blonde so bad?”

Brian’s eyes bulge. He swallows his mouthful of beer. “No, I don’t even get to.”

“Really?” Rob asks suspiciously.

“Really.” He stares straight at Rob, giving him a grave look.

“Then what is your motivation?”

Brian’s face relaxes into a grin. He starts talking glibly about the Mercer Estate. “Rob, if you were turned onto this place, you’d give Gary your notice and pack up your stuff, too.”

“No, I don’t think so.”

“No? You’d rather grovel to some jackass client to keep him from pulling his service account day after day?”

“A paycheck’s a paycheck.” Rob takes a sip of his drink.

“So okay, if given the choice, you would reject an expense-free luxury life?” Brian challenges him.

“There’s got to be some price to pay for that. Like abruptly giving up your life as you know it.”

***

Ambient music quivers softly throughout Black’s car. Becky is browsing Black’s music library. She appears quite content to have the ability to ask him questions at will, such as,

“Have you ever been married?”

“No, you?”

“No,” Becky says through a light laugh. “That seems like something I would’ve mentioned to you by now, knowing me.”

“That’s true.” He agrees.

“What did you used to do? Before all of this, I mean?” She glimpses up from the mp3 player at Black.

“I went to school and worked as an actuary for a life insurance company.”

“Hmm,” Becky hums in surprise, “interesting.”

“If you think I’m an asshole now, you should’ve known me back then.”

“Why do you say that?” She pries, combing through his diverse music library.

“Are you familiar with the occupation?” he asks her.

“Yes. An actuary is a person who brings a fake bomb on a plane, because it decreases the chances of there being another bomb on the plane.”

Black glances over at Becky with a slight smile. “Funny.”

“Thanks,” she whispers.

“Anyway, then about three years ago, I met Sam and... the rest is history.”

Becky nods and sees him take a lighter out of his pocket. “So where do you live, then?”

Black pulls a half-smoked joint out of his cup holder ashtray. “A place out on the edge of town.” He lights the joint.

***

“Yeah I mean, living on the property and helping out around there is part of the deal. But that’s a small price tag. There’s an open bar, all amenities, excellent food. The people there are cool as hell, and the place is crawling with women.” Back at Tiger’s, Brian flops back into his seat and picks up his beer.

“What kind of place is this?” Rob asks him.

“It’s an underground, club, I guess you could say.” He sips his beer, impervious to Rob’s disapproving glare.

“You guess? I don’t know, Brian. I really feel like you’re making a bad decision, here.”

“I think you’re blowing it out of proportion. Number one, this is not an irreversible decision.”

Rob exhales in comfort of the fact that his friend doesn’t necessarily view this as a permanent situation.

“And number two,” Brian adds, “I have every intention of keeping in touch and hanging out with all you guys. Nothing goes away except the things I want to leave behind.”

Upon hearing that Brian will still be around regularly, acceptance finally washes over Rob. “As long as you’re not totally falling off the radar.” His attitude lightens considerably. He picks up his drink.

“No, not at all.” Brian confirms, successfully putting the Rob issue to rest.

***

“So, this place where you live?” Becky interrogates Black behind the wheel. Beside him, his window is rolled down a couple inches.

“What about it?” He brings the joint up to his lips. It crackles when he takes a hit.

“Is it like a commune, or something?”

“No, not what you’re probably picturing.” Black offers Becky the joint. A thin curl of smoke escapes his mouth.

“No thanks.”

He blows a cloud of smoke out the window. “The property used to be a hunting lodge, like a weekend resort for game hunters. But the guy who owned the place started racking up gambling debts. Before he hit bottom, he sold the lodge to one of the members.” Black taps the joint into the ashtray. Its earthy aroma infuses the air.

“Who’s that?”

“Doesn’t really matter, the guy’s dead now. This was over fifty years ago.”

“Really?” Becky sets the mp3 player back down in Black’s console.

“Anyway, him and a few of the other members pitched in and redid the place. And in 1968, they started up a new club.”

“Do I ever get to see this place?” Becky cracks her window as smoke spreads through the car.

“Probably.”

“But you’re not gonna tell me when.”

“Of course not.”

Becky twists sideways in her seat. She confronts Black’s profile with a serious pout. “All right, then answer this for me.”

“What’s that?”

“How’d you know where I work?”

“Oh we’ve got surveillance software, hacking experts, all kinds of shit,” he answers nonchalantly. “There’s obviously GPS on that phone I gave you, too.”

Becky clenches her jaw at the extent of his resources, the sheer level at which he plays this so-called ‘game’.

Black seems oblivious to Becky’s astonishment. He takes another hit of the joint.

She collects herself enough to spit out a gasping reply. “Really?”

“Yeah, are you surprised?” He glances at her. “You wouldn’t believe the stuff we can find out about people.” Black snuffs his joint out in the ashtray. His focus reverts to the road. The meandering electronica song playing in the car drones on like a trippy backdrop to Becky’s unblinking pose.

“Huh, I guess you all take this game pretty seriously.”

“It’s all in fun.” He shrugs. “If something makes people happy and doesn’t cause any damage, then what’s the problem?”

chapters.title: Chapter 6
chapters.content:
Chapter 6

The next morning, Becky is seated at her office desk scrolling through work emails. She has a reflective glaze in her eyes. During their normal-life date, Black gave Becky enough insight for her to make an informed decision of whether to run like hell or choose to start a new chapter in life.

Becky looks up from the monitor. A stack of files lands on the corner of her desk. Her boss, Gary, steps back from her desk and slides his hands into the pockets of his black dress slacks.

“Now, I know you’re the newest person in the department, but I’m asking everybody to pitch in a little until we hire a replacement for Brian.”

“Oh, okay.” She reluctantly reaches for the stack of files.

“So I really need you to follow up on these accounts for me.”

With a sullen frown, Becky sets the files down by her keyboard. “I’ll let you know if I have any questions.”

“You do that.” Gary instructs her. He exits her office, leaving the door cracked. Becky sighs and flips open the first file on the stack. She skims through it.

Jackie pokes her head in the door. “How many did you get stuck with?”

“I don’t know.” Becky flips the file closed and runs her thumb down the side of the pile. “Half a dozen, I guess. Has anybody figured out what in the hell happened to Brian?”

“No.”

“Really?”

“Really. What are you doing for lunch?” Jackie asks.

“I think I’m gonna run home today.”

“Okay. Well, Gary’s making the rounds. I better get going.”

“See you later.”

Jackie disappears from the doorway. Becky continues glossing over the stack of Brian’s abandoned accounts. After a while, she pushes them aside and turns to her keyboard. She pulls up her bank on the computer and logs in. Becky clicks on the link to her checking account. She leans back in her desk chair, growing contemplative. She has enough money saved up to make it a year without a paycheck. Her gaze drifts from her checking account balance, over to the stack of Brian’s accounts, up to the clock in the corner of her monitor which reads 10:30 a.m.

***

Meanwhile, Hannah drinks the last of her fresh-squeezed orange juice and sets the empty glass down next to her banana peel. She directs her attention to Cade. “Let me borrow your seat, just for a minute. I’ve got a lower back spot.”

“Oh, I guess so.” Cade shifts over in the bubbling hot tub to the seat across from Black. That undesirable spot is wedged between two corner loungers that limit leg span room.

Hannah repositions until she’s satisfied with the jet that’s aimed at her lower back. “Ahh.” She briefly closes her eyes while adjusting to the jet’s pulse. Suddenly, Hannah’s eyes pop back open, bouncing back and forth between Cade and Black. “Before Cade gets back into his abduction blueprint, I thought you’d like to know that Brian happily returned home last night.” She broadcasts with gusto.

“You must be doing something right this time.”

Hannah ignores Cade’s remark and goes on. “Just to keep him on his toes, I had a little visit with him earlier this morning. Right,” she points to the pool, “over there.”

“About what?” Black asks.

“Me,” she tells him...

Hannah and Brian sit side by side in lounge chairs facing the pool. They each have a glass of fresh-squeezed orange juice. Across from them, the still pool water glistens under the rays of morning sun.

Hannah sets her banana down on the seat beside her. “Will said that everything went fine last night.”

“Yeah, it was all pretty much like I expected.” Brian reports.

“Good.” She abruptly switches the subject. “What type of porn do you generally watch, Brian?”

He thinks about it for a moment. “It’s not specific,” he frankly relays, “it’s kind of all over the place.”

“Mm-hmm, any niche, fetish?”

“Sure.” Brian chuckles at her. “All kinds of them.”

“Can you remember ever seeing the Profane Productions logo before?”

“Many, many times, yes.” Brian pauses in recollection. There’s a name associated with the production company. “Hannah Sedgwick is the elusive mastermind behind Profane Productions. I’ve read articles.” He stops talking and concentrates on Hannah with marked skepticism. “No.” He sees her furtive smile emerging. “No way.” Brian shakes his head. “You’re not Hannah Sedgwick.”

“Why, because that wouldn’t make any sense, or what?”

Brian hunches forward exhaling a rapt pant. “I don’t even know what to say. I was already ten kinds of intimidated by you, but. Hannah Sedgwick?” He gasps at the bombshell...

“You revealed that pretty early.” Cade notes.

“I thought that extra morsel would seal the deal, quell any lingering doubt.” Hannah reaches up out of the rippling water to tuck a stray strand of blonde hair behind her ear. “And you know, why keep it under wraps?”

“Yeah, you’re a producer, not a porn star.” Black smirks and drops deeper into the tub until his shoulders are submerged.

“Oh I’m a star, just not an actor. Besides, the only one who has a problem with it at all, is Random.”

“Anyway.” Cade cuts her off and turns to Black. “When we get back inside, can I swing by to go over a few things with you?”

“Bet you’ll be glad when this is over, tomorrow.” Hannah trades a sneer with Black.

“I have a feeling it won’t end there,” he tells her before answering Cade’s question. “But yeah, that’s fine.”

“Thank you.” Cade nods appreciatively.

Hannah stretches her tan arms over her head. “Well, I suppose I would’ve heard something if there was something to hear, but any word on Trip yet?”

“No. But I’m sure he’s getting by, at the very least.” Black presumes.

***

“Alive & Well”, a peculiar little song by Phantom Family Halo, thumps in the background of Trip’s room at Aunt Nelly’s Bed and Breakfast in Oklahoma. He’s sitting on the patchwork spread that covers the bed in his small room, flipping the page of the hardcover book he’s reading. Each page takes him longer to finish. Eventually his literary distraction fails him. Trip closes the book and places it on the knotty pine dresser beside him. His craving for true escapism draws him up off the bed and up to the bedroom window. Opaque white sheers are tied back on either side.

He stares out at the distant, vast farm fields veiled by overcast skies. Trip fixates on the heavy clouds in the sky, like they’re calling him to hunt down a filter. He backs away from the window and goes into the adjacent bathroom.

Trip flips on the light and closes the door behind him. The shabby chic bathroom has a prominent lavender color motif. He scans the bathroom sink vanity, stopping at an apothecary jar full of cotton swabs. Trip lifts the jar’s metal lid and digs out a couple of swabs.

He takes them back into his bedroom, over to the knotty pine dresser where his shoulder bag is lying. He reaches in and pulls out a small black bag. The unzipped bag reveals a few syringes inside. Trip stuffs the cotton swabs into the bag and keeps on gathering supplies.

He circles back to the nightstand, where his book is sitting beside his coffee mug from earlier that day. Inside the mug is a metal spoon. Trip snatches the filmy spoon out of his mug. He carries it into the bathroom.

Trip turns on the faucet and dispenses a pump of lavender-scented soap into his hand. He begins scrubbing the coffee film off the spoon, rinsing it off under the running water. There’s no doubt about the direction he’s heading.

***

“Where’s Becky?” Gary steps up to the WPC reception counter. Jackie transfers a call, hangs up the phone and looks at him.

“Um, she’s not in her office?” She checks the time on her computer. It’s 2:25 p.m.

“I just went in there to check in on her, and her light’s off.”

“She said she was going home for lunch.”

“It’s almost two-thirty.” He stresses.

“I guess she never came back from lunch.”

“What the hell is going on around here?” Gary throws up his hands. “First Brian and now Becky?”

Jackie stalls, unsure of what to tell him.

***

Meanwhile, Black is seated in front of his laptop inside his office at the Mercer Estate.

Cade is on a barstool behind him holding an open file folder. “Random will be down between the front seats, and you’ll be behind Jane with the blindfold.”

Black glances over his shoulder at Cade. “At that point, she’ll have her phone with her, then.”

“Yeah, it’ll be in the truck. But she won’t be able to get to it.”

“When are you putting the tracker on it?” Black turns to his computer and pulls up Becky’s location on a GPS map. She is not at WPC. He checks the clock on his screen. It’s 2:30 p.m., but she’s not at work.

“Reno’ll take care of it once we get her here.” Cade clarifies. “Her purse will end up back in her car.”

“Okay.” A twinge of concern crosses Black’s face when he realizes Becky’s at home. “Wait a minute.”

***

The television is on in the living room of Becky’s townhouse that afternoon. It sits across from her couch on a TV stand. The bottom shelves display vacation trinkets, books and candles.

She walks out of her bedroom with a basket of laundry. Two phones are sitting on the long table behind her couch. Her new phone begins ringing. She sees Black’s name displayed on the screen and answers the call. “Hello?”

“Why aren’t you at work?” Black asks on the other line.

“What?” Becky sets her laundry basket down on the floor.

“Why didn’t you go back to work, today?”

“How in the hell would you know that?” She wanders around to the front of her couch.

“The phone, Becky,” he tells her in an impatient voice.

“AH yes. You’re tracking my every move. How could I forget?”

“Tell me what’s going on.”

“I made another decision.” Becky timidly announces, sinking down onto her couch.

“To quit your job? What for?”

“I think it’s rational to assume that you do not have a traditional day job. So, how realistic would it be for me to advance in this game with one?”

“What is your point?”

“I’d like to speed things up a bit.” She admits.

“That’s not your call to make.”

“I realize that. But worst-case scenario, my job would take me back in a heartbeat.” Becky’s bold statement is underlined with plea.

“Why are you so sure?”

“Because Brian quit this week, so they’re already a person short.” She reveals and plunges back into the couch cushion...

Back in Black’s office, he’s on his laptop busily hacking into Becky’s home computer. Cade is no longer in there.

On the other line, Becky continues making her case to him. “And one of my co-workers knows that I went home for lunch. So I’d say I was sick, I stayed home.”

Black searches through Becky’s picture files and runs across one titled, ‘Me and Brian’. He clicks open the file, a picture of Becky with Brian. It’s a different image than the framed photo he briefly saw at her townhouse the night she made him a mojito.

“Listen Becky, it’s a little soon for you to be quitting your job. And why do I have to remind you that you’re not running the show?” Black opens a message box on his screen, below the picture of Becky and Brian. He starts typing a message to Hannah.

“Please, just let me do this.” She implores him.

“Why do you want to do this?” he asks and sends the message to Hannah. It reads, ‘send me a picture of Brian’.

“I’ve asked myself that. And I keep coming back to the same answer: why not? I’m twenty-nine, and I have never stepped outside of the box of normality. I’ve been doing exactly what’s expected of me ever since I was a kid. I’ve gone to school, held a job, paid my bills and been a good little citizen.”

The picture file from Hannah arrives promptly. It opens up to a shot of Brian, unconscious and lying on his stomach. He has a ball gag hanging from his neck. His hands and feet are bound to the legs of a weightlifting bench below.

“And it’s time.” Becky reasons. “It’s time that I make a choice that isn’t safe, for once. I know you hold the cards though, so please tell me it’s okay to just bite the bullet and do this.”

“Be ready to go at eight o’clock tonight.” He hangs up on Becky. The two pictures of Brian from two different sources are opened up on his laptop. Fixed on the screen, Black raises his fingertips to his cheeks. He covers his mouth, muttering, “Fuh-huh-ck...” through a short, disparaging laugh. Black runs his hands over his face and drops his palms to the desk.

***

The small dining room in Babe’s family’s farmhouse is a bit dated but squeaky clean. Its walls are a pale rust color and display a few old family portraits in ornate plaster frames. A plain chandelier hangs above the table full of home-cooked food.

Despite the sound of a TV in the next room, the rural house seems much too quiet for Trip. He looks across the table at Babe and takes in the comfort of her warm smile. She is seated between her younger brother, a slim eighteen-year-old with strawberry blonde hair, and her father, Ray, who’s in his late forties.

Fifteen massage tables are scattered around the dimly lit activity room at the Community Health Center that evening. Each table holds a volunteer, who is receiving a massage from one of the fifteen students. Mindfully placed room dividers offer sufficient privacy to the partially undressed volunteers. The delicate sound of a wind chime trickles through the air, courtesy of the meditation music playing in the room.

Jane Bostick bends sideways over her male volunteer’s firm, bare back. She glides her thumbs up the sides of his neck and applies a light pressure at the base of his head. Sweeping her thumbs outward, she moves them back down to his neck and repeats the motion. Jane serenely works through the final phase of the massage. She’s a coltish beauty in her late twenties with a lean build and dark glossy hair, which is up in a ponytail. Tonight, she’s comfortably dressed for her clinical in a pale pink, zipped hoodie and black cotton pants.

The class instructor, a somewhat frumpy and mellow woman in her fifties, ambles over to the doorway. She reaches for the dimmer switch on the wall near the door. “All right, students and guests, this concludes our session.” She bumps up the dimmer switch, gradually brightening the activity room lights. “I would like to thank all of our guests for volunteering your time for our clinical this evening. I hope that you all leave here feeling much more relaxed than when you arrived.”

A buzz of positive reactions swarms through the room, settling down into a low murmur.

“Take your time and just get up slowly.” Jane reaches for the shelf underneath the massage table. She pulls out a towel and wipes off her hands. Her ‘guest’ pushes himself up from the table.

He lifts his face up out of the head rest; it’s Reno.

“I’ll step away and give you some privacy to get dressed.” Jane offers.

Reno rolls onto his side, blinking to readjust to the light. He casually says, “No you’re fine.” Reno runs his hand through his hair. He has a genial smile on his face. A white sheet is draped over his bottom half, but his tan, muscular chest and arms are exposed. “I feel like I owe you dinner, now.”

Jane laughs at Reno, who pushes himself up into a sitting position. She discreetly inspects the tattoo on his chest while tossing her hand towel back down to the shelf below the massage table. “I’ll take that to mean I did a good job for you, then.”

“You could do me one better and hand me my clothes.” Reno refers to the metal folding chair nearby, where his grey slacks and white button-down shirt are draped over the back.

“No problem.” Jane turns to the folding chair and picks up his clothes. “I’m a little surprised that you volunteered for this in the first place.”

Reno lifts a curious brow as Jane winds back around to him. “Thank you.” He takes his clothing from her. “Why do you say that?” Reno lays his pants down on the table beside him.

“I was actually searching for some sign of tension but didn’t find any on you. You’re very relaxed.” She sits down in the metal folding chair and crosses her legs.

“Well, I got the tip to come here from one of my clients, Doctor Weaver.” He lies to her.

Jane lights up in recognition. “The school administrator?”

“That’s the one.” Reno starts putting on the white dress shirt.

“He’s a client of yours?” she asks.

“I manage his portfolio. Just met with him earlier in the week.” Reno pulls the shirt on over his shoulders and buttons it up.

“So, you handle investments?”

“Yes I do.”

Jane inquisitively scans up and down between Reno’s face and chest. She sees a very attractive, professional man sporting an obscure tattoo. The dichotomy compels her to ask him about it. “Travesty, huh?”

Remaining reticent, Reno finishes buttoning up his shirt. “Yeah, I have to keep it under wraps, though.”

The two of them lock eyes. Jane nods in understanding.

“So, I was obviously kidding about dinner earlier, but how about a glass of wine?” Reno buttons his cuffs. “I think I saw someplace a few doors down from here.”

“Uh yeah, you did. It’s called Between the Vines.”

“That sounds right.” He shrugs. “What do you think?”

“Sure.” Jane comfortably accepts Reno’s proposition. “Why not?”
